docs.title: Why AVSecTester
docs.text:
AVSecTester tests attacks and defenses the way they would play out on the road: in a vehicle that keeps driving.

  • Closed-loop rollouts. Open-loop evaluation can rate a driving system highly even when it ignores what is in front of it [3]. AVSecTester rolls the driving system out in closed loop. Its commands move the vehicle, the next camera frame follows from that motion, and the attack acts at every step. You see whether the vehicle actually stops, brakes or crashes.
  • Comparable, reproducible experiments. Every attack runs through the same workflow and one YAML file configures the whole experiment. Clean and attacked runs start from the same state, and every run is logged, so results can be re-evaluated, compared across attacks and resumed after an interruption.
  • Bring your own code. Add attacks, driving systems or metrics in your own package and reference them from the YAML, without changing the framework.

docs.title: What you can do with it
docs.text:
AVSecTester is built for people who develop and evaluate autonomous-vehicle security: researchers who design attacks and defenses, and engineers who test driving systems against them.

Defense evaluation is planned. See Defenses.

docs.title: Test a new attack
docs.text:
Does your attack change how the vehicle drives, not just a detection score? Write it in Python or start from a supplied attack: choose where it applies, optimize it offline and act at every decision. Each test segment runs clean and attacked from the same start.

Attacks

docs.title: Stress-test a driving system
docs.text:
How does your driving system behave under known attacks? Wrap it as an AVStack. A DrivingAdapter exposes its components to attacks. Run supplied attacks over many drives and get paired reports of stopping, braking, stop-line and collision outcomes.

Driving systems

docs.title: Optimize an attack
docs.text:
How strong can an attack get? Optimize a patch with gradients through the driving system's own model (white-box, PGD [1]) or with queries only (black-box, NES [4]), then test it on new scenes.

Optimization

docs.title: Record and replay runs
docs.text:
Every run saves the camera input the driving system received, its outputs and the vehicle's physical state. Measure, compare, replay and export frames later without running the simulator again.

Evaluation

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Choose where to drive. Use real-world drives reconstructed with NuRec or CARLA scenarios, and a supplied driving system or your own.
  2. Choose or write an attack. It selects the segments it applies to, prepares its artifacts in an offline phase and acts on the world, the sensors or the driving system in the online phase.
  3. Run and compare. One command prepares the attack, runs clean and attacked treatments of every test segment in closed loop and writes metrics and an HTML report.
# configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml, abridged
dataset:
  type: NuRecDataset            # reconstructed real-world drives
simulator:
  type: NuRecSimulator          # commands move the vehicle and the next frame follows
avstack:
  type: RuleBasedAVStack        # or AlpamayoAVStack, or your own AVStack
attacks:
  noise_detector_pgd:
    type: StopSignPatchAttack   # or your own Attack
    options:
      initial_patch: low_frequency_noise
      optimization: ...         # white-box attack (algorithm used: PGD)
runs:
  treatments:
    - {name: clean, attack_name: no_patch}
    - {name: noise_detector_pgd, attack_name: noise_detector_pgd}

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml

docs.title: Before you try
docs.text:
• Requirements. Linux with NVIDIA GPUs, Docker Compose and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Experiments run in the supplied Docker images. NuRec scenes, NRE images and model weights are downloaded separately and need NGC and Hugging Face access. See Installation.
  • Status. AVSecTester is an early research release. The supported simulator and driving-system combinations are listed in Supported configurations.

docs.title: Responsible use
docs.text:
AVSecTester is intended for research, education and authorized security testing of autonomous driving systems. Its attacks run in simulation and on recorded or reconstructed data.

  • Do not use the attacks, or physical artifacts produced with them, against vehicles, road infrastructure or systems that you do not own or are not authorized to test, and never on public roads.
  • Follow applicable laws and the terms of the datasets and models you use.
  • If you find a vulnerability in a real system, report it to the affected vendor before publishing it.
  • Results in simulation do not establish that a real vehicle is safe or unsafe. The software is provided under the MIT License, without warranty.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Audience: Experiment authors and contributors.

Outcome: Understand framework components, dependency layers and isolation.

Prerequisites: None.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
AVSecTester combines recorded data or scenario recipes, a simulator, a driving system and attacks. Each simulator and driving-system integration retains its native implementation.

Component Responsibility Dataset Recorded frames, recipes and semantic maps Simulator Reusable settings and capability declarations SimulatorRuntime One active world, clock, actors and sensor captures AVStack Driving inference and per-run history ObservationPipeline Model-visible sensor processing, localization and observation hooks DrivingAdapter AVStack construction and component/scorer bindings Attack Parameters, segment selection and offline preparation AttackRuntime One run's online phase ClosedLoopServices Isolated sensor, render, component and rollout requests ScenarioView One scenario's timeline, frame data and selection reasons Experiment Preparation, treatment execution and persistence HookSet Ordered callbacks, lifecycle and run-scoped random generators RunLog Independent step and event snapshots Metric Measurements from recorded comparison groups

The runtime reference defines decision order and recorded evidence. The Python API lists public modules and contracts.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
Term Meaning Scenario One dataset scene or simulator recipe Segment A scenario window with attack-owned user_data Unit A distinct segment, including its complete user_data Treatment A named attack/environment setting Comparison group A unit and seed with the applicable treatments Offline phase Preparation of artifacts before execution. It may be a no-op Online phase An AttackRuntime's setup, step and stop lifecycle. It may be a no-op Attack action A modification requested by an attacker Command A driving-system output or the command executed by the simulator Attack impact A measured consequence for driving Metabuilder An attack's build_metadata method for scenario-segment selection Metadata Selected segments and their attack-owned data Artifact Prepared data reused by online phases Environment World settings and sensor corruptions Unattacked treatment A treatment with no enabled attack NRE NVIDIA Neural Rendering Engine CATK Closest Among Top-K

See attacks for implementing the two phases and evaluation for comparing treatments.

docs.text:
Paths are relative to avsectester/.

Directory Responsibility ./ Shared records, validation, serialization, type paths and CLI entry points geometry/ Camera models, poses, projection and ray/mesh geometry datasets/ Stateless recordings and recipes maps/ Semantic records and map readers rendering/ Assets, surfaces, textures, harmonizers and composition closed_loop/ Hooks, environments and sensor corruptions closed_loop/simulators/ Contracts, recorded playback, dynamics, navigation, ground contact and object composition closed_loop/simulators/carla/ CARLA world and sensor integration closed_loop/simulators/nurec/ NuRec rendering, traffic.py sessions and server.py local services closed_loop/avstacks/ Driving interfaces and DrivingAdapter closed_loop/avstacks/implemented/ Supplied driving systems, including modules/ attack/ Attack contracts and structured offline_report outputs attack/insertion/ Assets, placement, visibility and insertion actions attack/optimization/ Optimization interfaces, algorithms and scorer bindings runlog/ Recording and reading steps, events and payloads execution/ Runner, services and frame-data caching evaluation/ Metrics, comparison groups, reports and plots implemented_attacks/ One concrete attack per snake_case class directory experiment/ Configuration, preparation, execution and saved outputs

Simulator and AVStack package initializers expose interfaces. Import implementations from their own modules. User implementations live in their own packages. See driving systems and attacks.

docs.title: Dependency layers
docs.text:
Internal imports point to the same layer or a lower layer, including imports inside functions. The declared type-only exception below permits annotations without a runtime dependency.

Layer Modules Allowed internal imports L0 geometry/, validation.py, type_paths.py, serialization.py L0 L0′ data_types.py L0–L0′ L1 datasets/, maps/, rendering/ L0–L1 L2 closed_loop/ L0–L2 L3 attack/, runlog/ L0–L3 L4 execution/ L0–L4 L5 evaluation/ L0–L5 L6 implemented_attacks/ L0–L6 L7 experiment/ L0–L7 L8 cli.py L0–L8 Importer Imported module Condition avsectester.attack.attack avsectester.execution.services TYPE_CHECKING

Map readers do not depend on datasets. Rendering does not depend on simulators or attacks. Generic attack tools do not import concrete attacks, and concrete attacks do not import one another. Optional SDK, model and GPU imports stay inside their owning implementations.

docs.title: World ownership
docs.text:
A runtime's world_key identifies its mutable world. Runtimes sharing an external world use the same key. Within a process, claim_world permits nested claims by the same owner and rejects another owner immediately. The caller closes native resources before releasing its claim.

exclusive also rejects nested operations on the same runtime. Claims do not coordinate separate processes. See the runtime contracts.

docs.text:
Isolation means a run has its own runtime state and recorded snapshots. Comparison groups are defined in Terms.

See experiment workflows for resource scopes and evaluation for grouping and measurements.

Check API names, signatures, YAML keys, defaults and paths against source. Use Simulator for configuration, SimulatorRuntime for a live world, AVStack for driving, DrivingAdapter for bindings, HookSet for hooks, environment for world or sensor settings, and metabuilder for segment selection.

Use offline phase and online phase for attack lifecycle phases. Call an attack that uses model gradients a white-box attack and one that only queries rollouts a black-box attack. Identify its optimizer only as "algorithm used: PGD" or "algorithm used: NES".

Use English, sentence-case headings and prose lines of at most 100 characters. Tables, code and URLs are exempt. Task pages begin with Audience, Outcome and Prerequisites. Guides end with Next steps.

Describe behavior and defaults. Keep measurements, investigation notes and version histories out of the documentation. Mark missing capabilities with Not yet implemented. and link to a specific heading in TODO.

Self-contained examples place <!-- runnable --> immediately before their code fence. Python and py blocks execute offline. Runnable YAML blocks load as complete experiment configurations. External-service examples state their prerequisites. Other Python blocks must parse and use resolvable framework imports.

Public modules declare __all__. The API reference lists exactly those names with checked signatures. Internal modules are implementation details.

After changing a public docstring, follow the generator command in Repository tools.

The project site publishes docs/ unchanged under /docs/, except the TODO page, which stays on GitHub. Site links to it open it there. Every page must render correctly both on GitHub and on the site, so use only standard Markdown and GitHub tables. Do not use Material for MkDocs syntax such as admonitions or content tabs. Add every new docs page to nav in website/mkdocs.yml. The strict site build fails on omitted pages. To preview the site, create a separate virtual environment, run pip install -r website/requirements.txt and then mkdocs serve -f website/mkdocs.yml. This is a documentation tool and runs outside the Compose experiment services.

docs.title: Image object insertion
docs.text:
Audience: Users inserting an asset into captured camera images.

Outcome: Run ObjectInsertionAttack on a selected simulator configuration.

Prerequisites: Installation and the selected dataset.

docs.title: Configurations
docs.text:
docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester run configs/carla_object_insertion.yaml
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/nurec_object_insertion.yaml
docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester run configs/nuscenes_object_insertion.yaml

The NuRec configuration selects the following asset and placement:

type: ObjectInsertionAttack
options:
  decision_steps: 20
  max_segments: 1
  assets:
    type: avsectester.implemented_attacks.object_insertion_attack.assets:SignAsset
  sensor: camera_front_wide_120fov
  placement:
    type: avsectester.attack.insertion.placement:WorldPlacement
    options: {position_m: [28.0, -3.0, 0.0]}
  orientation:
    type: avsectester.attack.insertion.placement:Orientation
    options: {mode: face_ego}
  placement_relative_to_ego_origin: true

The relative placement is resolved once from the initial ego actor/rig origin and then remains fixed in world coordinates. Asset origins, sizes and placement constraints are defined in the Python API.

docs.title: Offline phase
docs.text: The attack selects eligible camera views without changing their inputs. Its offline phase retains the configured asset. Attack authoring responsibilities are in Writing attacks.

docs.title: Online phase
docs.text:
Each runtime composites the asset into the selected captured image. This does not create a collidable actor. Simulators describes insertion and occlusion behavior. nuScenes uses recorded playback rather than a reactive driving world.

This attack modifies only the selected camera image. Not yet implemented. Insertion into LiDAR or other non-camera sensors. See Non-camera insertion.

docs.title: Harmonization and custom assets
docs.text:
Use ExposureHarmonizer for differentiable exposure matching. Harmonizer formulas, nominal textures, shared deployment/optimization calculations and custom interfaces are in the Python API.

This self-contained example constructs an insertion action with a custom plane:

import numpy as np
from avsectester.attack.insertion import Insertion, InsertionAttackAction, PatchCompositor, PlaneAsset
from avsectester.attack.insertion.placement import WorldPlacement
from avsectester.rendering import ExposureHarmonizer

asset = PlaneAsset(np.full((16, 32, 4), 255, dtype=np.uint8), width_m=1.0, height_m=0.5)
insertion = Insertion("banner", asset, WorldPlacement((10.0, 0.0, 1.5)))
action = InsertionAttackAction(
    "front", insertion, PatchCompositor(ExposureHarmonizer(), soften=0.0))
assert action.insertion.asset.planes()[0].texture.shape == (16, 32, 4)

Return the action from an attack runtime as described in Writing attacks.

docs.title: Offline phase
docs.text: The attack selects decision windows. Its offline phase returns no artifact. Selection and deployment budgets follow Writing attacks.

docs.title: Online phase
docs.text: Each runtime inserts a synthetic perception detection at perception.post. The physical world contains no corresponding actor. The same decision then continues through the driving system. Stage order is defined in Runtime.

docs.title: Physical patch
docs.text:
Audience: Users deploying or optimizing a texture patch.

Outcome: Run a selected CARLA or NuRec PatchAttack configuration.

Prerequisites: Installation for the chosen simulator.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester run configs/carla_patch.yaml
docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester run configs/carla_patch_optimized.yaml
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/nurec_patch.yaml

Each configuration selects and prepares its own segments. The NuRec configuration includes:

type: PatchAttack
options:
  decision_steps: 20
  max_windows: 1
  sensor: camera_front_wide_120fov
  width_m: 1.0
  height_m: 0.5
  max_distance: 30.0
  candidate_hosts: ['15']
  hosts_per_window: 1
  assets:
    type: avsectester.rendering.textures:CheckerboardTexture
    options: {size: 256, cells: 8}

Texture and placement parameters are listed in the Python API. A Python texture object can provide RGBA pixels directly:

import numpy as np
from avsectester.implemented_attacks.patch_attack import PatchAttack

class SolidTexture:
    def rgba(self):
        return np.full((32, 64, 4), (255, 64, 0, 255), dtype=np.uint8)

attack = PatchAttack(decision_steps=5, assets=SolidTexture())

docs.title: Offline phase
docs.text: Selection ranks candidate hosts within each eligible window. Without optimization, the input texture becomes the artifact. An optimization option prepares a texture using the selected training segments and configured scorer. See Optimization.

docs.title: Online phase
docs.text:
The runtime receives the explicit texture artifact. CARLA uses a native physical prop. NuRec composites into the selected camera capture. Their geometry and occlusion behavior are described in Simulators.

Scaling a CARLA prop mesh to arbitrary requested panel dimensions is Not yet implemented. See Physical patch geometry.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Use the recorded camera input, deployment receipts and driving metrics described in Evaluation. The example overview explains the distinction between workflow execution and measured attack impact.

The carla_patch_optimized.yaml configuration uses a white-box attack (algorithm used: PGD) through the mmdet.rpn_objectness scorer bound by modular_driving_adapter.

docs.title: Speed-feedback attack
docs.text:
Audience: Users studying per-run feedback state.

Outcome: Inspect a model-visible speed bias separately from physical motion.

Prerequisites: Installation for NuRec.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/nurec_speed_feedback.yaml

The supplied configuration uses:

type: SpeedFeedbackAttack
options:
  decision_steps: 20
  max_segments: 2
  target_speed: 12.0
  gain: 0.1
  max_bias: 5.0

Parameter defaults and constraints are in the Python API.

docs.title: Offline phase
docs.text: The attack selects decision windows. Its offline phase returns no artifact. See Writing attacks for the common lifecycle.

docs.title: Online phase
docs.text:
A fresh runtime maintains a bounded nonnegative speed bias from physical-state feedback and modifies Observation.ego_speed at the observation stage. It records speed_bias in each decision's outputs. The physical state remains separate in the RunLog.

Alpamayo derives its speed inputs from pose history, so this observation-field change does not alter those inputs. Driving-system inputs are described in Driving systems.

Feedback driven by another actor's perception history is Not yet implemented. See Actor-aware adaptive attack.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Compare the recorded speed_bias, model observation and physical motion with the configured Evaluation. The example overview explains impact assessment.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Read Runtime and Writing attacks.

docs.title: Stop-sign patch attack
docs.text:
Audience: Users studying stop-sign patches in reconstructed NuRec scenes.

Outcome: Prepare fixed or optimized replica textures, run test treatments and inspect reports.

Prerequisites: Installation, NuRec scene archives and the driving-system weights referenced by the chosen configuration.

docs.title: Choose a configuration
docs.text:
The optimized treatments use the following attack type and algorithm. Each configuration also includes unoptimized controls.

Configuration Driving system Attack type Algorithm used nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml RuleBasedAVStack white-box attack PGD nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2604.yaml RuleBasedAVStack white-box attack PGD nurec_stop_sign_patch_alpamayo_2601.yaml AlpamayoAVStack black-box attack NES nurec_stop_sign_patch_alpamayo_2604.yaml AlpamayoAVStack black-box attack NES

Run from the repository root after configuring data and weights:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_alpamayo_2601.yaml

Service management follows the CLI service lifecycle. See Examples for the complete supplied configuration list.

The modular configurations use RuleBasedAVStack. The suffixes _2601 and _2604 refer to NuRec 26.01 and 26.04, stored under data/nurec/26.01_release and data/nurec/26.04_release. See Installation for weights.

docs.title: Treatments
docs.text:
The modular configurations contain the detector-optimized treatments. The Alpamayo configurations contain the rollout-optimized treatments. Both include the same controls.

Treatment Initial patch Optimized Attack type clean Unpatched replica No Baseline white White No Fixed patch black Black No Fixed patch noise Low-frequency noise No Fixed patch white_detector_pgd White Yes white-box attack black_detector_pgd Black Yes white-box attack noise_detector_pgd Low-frequency noise Yes white-box attack white_rollout_nes White Yes black-box attack black_rollout_nes Black Yes black-box attack noise_rollout_nes Low-frequency noise Yes black-box attack

Each attack has an offline phase and an online phase. With no optimization, the offline phase returns the initial texture. The online phase inserts that texture through the same placement path used during optimization. The clean treatment runs the no_patch attack, which uses initial_patch: none and cannot be optimized, so every treatment shows the same inserted replica and differs only in its patch.

low_frequency_noise draws independent color values on a grid of one value per noise_cell_texels face texels, default 32, and upsamples them bicubically. Its color patches stay visible at the small image sizes of an approaching camera, where per-texel noise averages to gray.

docs.title: Selection and placement
docs.text:
The selector uses the mapped stop sign, its stop-sign stop line and the recorded ego route. It chooses at most one approach per scene, from the entering side and facing the sign. The route must pass within 3 m of the line and contain a recorded speed below 0.5 m/s within 15 m before it.

The Alpamayo configurations set approach_m: 100 and min_approach_m: 60. The modular configurations use the defaults of 50 m and 20 m. The selector waits for required recorded history and includes hold_steps hold decisions, with a default of 20. A start closer than min_approach_m is rejected. Constructor defaults are in the stop-sign attack API.

The runtime inserts a post-free canonical MUTCD R1-1 replica face over the reconstructed sign. The mask_path binary mask selects which face-texture colors form the patch. The default rp2_bars.png places bars above and below STOP. face_interior.png is the packaged alternative. Artifacts keep the face alpha and all colors outside the mask.

The default placement is upright with a standard-size face. Map modes are alternatives:

Option Behavior face_orientation="upright" Use the horizontal projection of the annotated face normal and world +Z as up face_orientation="map" Preserve the annotated rotation, including tilt face_size="mutcd_standard" Select the width closest to annotated height from 0.762, 0.914 and 1.219 m face_size="map_width" Use the annotated width width_scale=1.1 Multiply the selected face width. Height follows the texture aspect ratio offset_m=0.10 Move the replica face center along the selected forward normal

The annotation supplies the center and yaw. Position or yaw errors can expose the reconstructed sign around the replica's edges at close range. The attack does not correct those annotations. The simulator's occlusion_tolerance_m handles occlusion. See Simulators.

The configurations use ExposureHarmonizer(reference="under"). Its gain is estimated from the reconstructed sign and the unpatched nominal replica, then applied to each patch. The same differentiable calculation is used for optimization and deployment. Formulas and constraints are in the harmonizer API.

docs.title: Training and test segments
docs.text:
All attacks select metadata before the shared split is formed. The supplied settings are:

split:
  train_segments: 5
  seed: 0
  execute: [test]

This needs at least six selected approaches: five training units and at least one test unit. See split configuration for unit identity, allocation and training input rules.

docs.title: Prepare the white-box attack
docs.text:
The white-box attack uses the driving system's YOLOX detector through avstack.bindings. Algorithm used: PGD. rule_based_driving_adapter declares rule_based.detection_confidence, the camera and decision threshold. A SessionScorer reuses it for calibration and optimization. The driving-system guide describes the binding behavior.

The driving system stops once the detector fires, so the patch must suppress every detection until the vehicle can no longer stop before the line. Training therefore covers recorded frames by route distance to the stop line, from the farthest frame where the unpatched replica reaches the decision threshold down to v² / (2 × braking_deceleration_mps2). v is the recorded speed at the segment start. braking_deceleration_mps2 is the driving system's strongest braking and defaults to 6 m/s², the RuleBasedAVStack planner limit. The sign-face projection defines the target box. Frames below min_visible_pixels are skipped. Its default is 100 visible replica pixels.

The configurations use all five training segments, every eligible frame (samples_per_scene: all), epochs: 100, batch_size: 16, tv_weight: 0.3 and step size 4/255. An integer samples_per_scene of at least four instead selects that many time-uniform frames per segment. Every selected frame is a training sample. Validation, when needed, uses separate segments from the data split.

The objective is HideBelowThreshold: max(0, s − (τ − m)) for detector confidence s, the driving system's decision threshold τ and confidence_margin m, default 0.1. One detection is enough for the driving system to stop, so frames already below τ − m stop contributing and the updates concentrate on frames that would still be detected. The margin absorbs differences between recorded training views and closed-loop views.

PGD's tv_weight adds a smoothness term to the detector loss, so the patch keeps structure that survives printing and camera sampling. The term is the mean Charbonnier RGB distance, sqrt(||c_p - c_q||² + ε²) - ε with ε = 0.001, over vertically and horizontally adjacent texels that are both inside the mask. Pairs across the patch outline are excluded, so a uniform patch has zero smoothness cost against the red face.

The offline report contains calibration and sample tables, the pgd_objective series, the final patch_smoothness, and initial/optimized replica textures. pgd_objective records the mean training hinge objective per epoch, excluding the smoothness term, at epochs 1 through epochs. After optimization every training frame is scored for the clean reconstruction, unpatched replica, initial patch and optimized patch. detected_frame_fraction and max_confidence summarize the optimized patch, and detection rates are binned by route distance to the stop line. The configurations set progress_interval: 10 to score the current patch on every training frame every 10 epochs and after the last epoch. The option defaults to 1. The training_progress table and its series record the full-set hinge loss, detected fraction and detected fraction per 10 m bin. Epoch 0 is the initial patch. Optimization tools explains report usage.

docs.title: Prepare the black-box attack
docs.text:
The black-box attack minimizes the mean stop-command distance over retained training segments. Algorithm used: NES.

A stop command is a decision whose timestamped planned trajectory has an adjacent-waypoint horizontal speed below stop_speed_mps, default 0.5 m/s. Stop-command distance is the horizontal distance from the ego origin to the sign-face center at the first such decision, before passing the sign. Only decisions with (ego_position − sign_center) · sign_x > 0 count, where sign_x is the first column of sign_pose. A rollout that passes the sign without a stop command scores 0. A rollout whose decisions run out before either event scores its remaining distance to the sign after the last decision, so ending early is not rewarded. The outcome column records which case applies.

Calibration evaluates the unpatched replica once per training segment, in metadata order. A segment is retained only if it issues a stop command at step min_stop_command_step or later, default 5, before passing the sign. Segments with an earlier command, no command before passing or decisions that run out first are excluded with a reason. Calibration stops after max_training_segments retained segments, or uses every eligible training segment when this limit is None. Calibration raises ValueError if no segment is retained.

Each candidate starts at each retained segment's recorded origin and runs for at most segment.decision_steps decisions. It ends when the first stop command is issued or the ego passes the sign. The scalar score is the mean stop-command distance across those segments.

The search variables are RGB offsets on a grid with one cell per noise_cell_texels face texels, default 32. Bicubic upsampling maps these offsets to the texture. Only masked RGB changes, and alpha and colors outside the mask stay fixed. No smoothness term is added.

The supplied configurations retain at most two training segments, set stop_speed_mps: 0.5 and min_stop_command_step: 5, and use steps: 10, population_size: 8, sigma: 0.15, learning_rate: 0.1, batch_size: 1 and seed: 0. The candidate query budget is:

retained training segments × (1 + steps × (population_size + 1))

Calibration adds one rollout per examined segment.

The offline report contains a calibration table with selection reasons, a rollouts table with per-query distances and run details, the stop_command_distance_m series, and initial and optimized textures. final_stop_command_distance_m is the final texture's evaluated mean distance. No additional rollout is used for that value. The attack API describes the optimization options.

docs.title: Reuse segments and resume
docs.text:
Use metadata.save to export selected units, or metadata.load to share a user-created selection. These settings and content-hash compatibility are defined by Metadata configuration. Saving a selection does not reuse optimized textures across driving systems.

Resume interrupted work with:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml --resume

Completed attack offline phases and matching completed runs are reused. Unfinished work follows the experiment resume workflow.

docs.title: Run from Python
docs.text:
To run the workflow from Python, open local_services around preparation and execution, or start NRE with nre serve first. Save this module as my_module.py in the repository root, which is the container's working directory:

from avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.nurec.server import local_services
from avsectester.experiment import Experiment, evaluate, load_configuration

def run(configuration_path, nre_gpu):
    configuration = load_configuration(configuration_path)
    Experiment.validate(configuration)
    with local_services(configuration.dataset, configuration.simulator,
                        nre_gpu=nre_gpu, log=print):
        prepared = Experiment.prepare(configuration)
        result = Experiment.execute(prepared)
        return evaluate(result, configuration)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run("configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml", nre_gpu=None)

See manual NRE commands for reusable services. Run a Python module through the same Compose environment:

docker compose run --rm --entrypoint python nurec-experiment -m my_module

docs.title: Optional reactive traffic
docs.text: Add simulator.options.traffic with type avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.nurec:AlpaSimTraffic and pass --trafficsim-models models/alpasim-trafficsim to run. It manages the local traffic service alongside NRE. The Simulator guide defines behavior and restrictions. Prepare the traffic image and weights following Installation.

docs.title: Evaluate and plot
docs.text:
Evaluate saved runs and generate stop-line plots:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment evaluate configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml
docker compose run --rm --entrypoint python nurec-experiment -m scripts.visualization.plot_stop_line_approaches configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml

The CLI reference defines the HTML and structured-output locations. Evaluation defines the stop-line, driving and reasoning metrics. RuleBasedAVStack has no reasoning text, so its configuration omits ReasoningPhraseRate.

docs.title: Custom metric example
docs.text:
ReplicaVisibility demonstrates an importable Metric outside the built-in metric registry. Its evaluate reads saved capture evidence and returns visible_steps. describe supplies the field's meaning and unit. A treatment without a replica has an unavailable value. A decision counts as visible when the replica reaches min_visible_pixels in at least one selected camera. By default camera_ids selects every camera that recorded the replica.

Reference the class by its full path, as in the supplied YAML:

evaluation:
  metrics:
    - type: avsectester.implemented_attacks.stop_sign_patch_attack.metrics:ReplicaVisibility

For a user metric, implement the same public methods in your own package and use its package.module:Class path. See the metric authoring guide for that interface, and the supplied implementation for a concrete example.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Audience: Users setting up an experiment environment.

Outcome: Prepare Compose services, data and model weights.

Prerequisites: Linux, NVIDIA GPUs, Docker Compose and NVIDIA Container Toolkit.

Use an NGC account for NRE images and obtain Hugging Face access to the selected NuRec dataset and Alpamayo checkpoint. Configure NVIDIA Container Toolkit as Docker's default runtime:

sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker --set-as-default
sudo systemctl restart docker

docs.title: Repository and Compose settings
docs.text:
Clone the checkout and initialize the native driving-system submodules:

git clone https://github.com/AVSecProject/AVSecTester.git
cd AVSecTester
git -c url.https://github.com/.insteadOf=git@github.com: submodule update --init --depth 1 -- \
  third_party/avstack-core third_party/avstack-api third_party/lib-avstack-carla
git -C third_party/avstack-core -c url.https://github.com/.insteadOf=git@github.com: \
  submodule update --init --depth 1 -- third_party/mmdetection third_party/mmdetection3d
scripts/preparation/write_compose_env.sh

The script writes .env with the repository path, user/group IDs, Docker socket group, Docker executable and GPU selections. It refuses to overwrite an existing file unless --force is supplied. Choose available host GPUs in .env: CARLA_SERVER_GPU, CARLA_EXPERIMENT_GPU and NUREC_GPU each default to 0.

Compose service Image Purpose carla-server carlasim/carla:0.9.16 CARLA server carla-experiment avsectester:carla CARLA driving-system environment nurec-experiment avsectester:nurec NuRec, AlpaSim controller and Alpamayo environment

The checkout is bind-mounted at its host absolute path. Experiments run as the configured user. Files written below the checkout are available on the host. Rebuild images after changing dependencies. Checkout code is read through PYTHONPATH.

docs.title: External data and models
docs.text:
For files outside the checkout, create an ignored docker-compose.override.yml that mounts the same absolute directories into every service that reads those external data or model files. For example, mount them into nurec-experiment:

services:
  nurec-experiment:
    volumes:
      - /srv/av-data:/srv/av-data:ro
      - /srv/models:/srv/models:ro

Link data and weights into the repository, or configure their paths directly:

mkdir -p data models
ln -s /srv/av-data/nurec data/nurec
ln -s /srv/models/Alpamayo-1.5-10B models/Alpamayo-1.5-10B

NuRec service containers mount the resolved archive and probe paths from the host. These paths must have the same absolute names on the host and in nurec-experiment. The service mounts the Docker socket and CLI to start sibling containers.

docs.title: CARLA environment
docs.text:
Fetch the avstack CARLA and nuScenes perception checkpoints and build the experiment image:

scripts/preparation/fetch_models.sh
docker compose build carla-experiment
docker compose up -d carla-server carla-experiment
docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester version

The image provides the native avstack and detector dependencies. Model files live under models/checkpoints, models/work_dirs and models/work_dirs_2d. Dockerfile creates the corresponding links inside the image.

CARLA uses host networking with RPC port 2000 and traffic-manager port 8000. Select the server and experiment host GPUs through .env. Model device indexes address GPUs visible in the experiment container. Stop the services with docker compose down.

docs.title: CARLA semantic maps
docs.text:
Map export is optional. With carla-server running, export Town03 and set the dataset's dataset.options.map_directory: ../data/carla_maps:

docker compose exec carla-experiment python -m scripts.preparation.export_carla_maps \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 2000 --town Town03 --output data/carla_maps

The files are written into the mounted checkout. Map use and unavailable-map behavior are described in Datasets.

docs.title: NuRec environment
docs.text:
Build the NuRec image and authenticate to the NRE image registry:

docker login nvcr.io
docker pull nvcr.io/nvidia/nre/nre-ga:26.04
docker compose build nurec-experiment
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment version

nurec-experiment uses the nurec profile, so ordinary docker compose up does not start it. An explicit docker compose run enables it. The image provides the Python 3.12 AlpaSim workspace and imports this checkout without installing the avsectester package, which requires Python 3.11.

Obtain access to the NuRec dataset and place the single-scene example at data/nurec/023b7fcc-671c-40e3-9bd2-c66b0b073fbc/023b7fcc-671c-40e3-9bd2-c66b0b073fbc.usdz. Stop-sign configurations use data/nurec/26.01_release or data/nurec/26.04_release. Place the nuScenes v1.0-trainval release under data/nuscenes, containing samples/, sweeps/, maps/ and v1.0-trainval/. The configuration data column lists data and weights for each workflow. dataroot or usdz_paths can select other locations.

The run command manages compatible NRE and trafficsim services automatically. See Service lifecycle. For manual service reuse, see NRE commands.

docs.title: Alpamayo weights
docs.text:
Set HF_TOKEN in your shell to a Hugging Face token with checkpoint access, then download:

export HF_TOKEN=YOUR_HUGGING_FACE_TOKEN
docker compose run --rm -e HF_TOKEN --entrypoint hf nurec-experiment \
  download nvidia/Alpamayo-1.5-10B --local-dir models/Alpamayo-1.5-10B

The supplied configurations set avstack.options.checkpoint_path. For a configuration that relies on AVSECTESTER_ALPAMAYO_CHECKPOINT, explicitly forward the variable to the Compose run:

export AVSECTESTER_ALPAMAYO_CHECKPOINT=/srv/models/Alpamayo-1.5-10B
docker compose run --rm -e AVSECTESTER_ALPAMAYO_CHECKPOINT nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml

The path must exist inside the experiment container. Driving systems describes model loading.

docs.title: YOLOX detector weights
docs.text:
The nurec image includes YOLOX. The rule-based driving system uses the COCO YOLOX-m checkpoint:

mkdir -p models
curl --fail --location \
  https://github.com/Megvii-BaseDetection/YOLOX/releases/download/0.1.1rc0/yolox_m.pth \
  --output models/yolox_m.pth

This is the local weights_path in the supplied modular stop-sign configurations. The framework does not fetch this checkpoint during a run.

docs.title: Reactive traffic weights and image
docs.text:
Build nurec-experiment first, then the CATK image that extends it:

docker build --target trafficsim -t avsectester:trafficsim .

Download the four weights files into models/alpasim-trafficsim:

traffic_models_dir=models/alpasim-trafficsim
traffic_models_url=https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/NVlabs/alpasim/affc2eab209fa43bdfa2f26c0f8d437922d78a68/data/trafficsim-models
mkdir -p "$traffic_models_dir/catk_v120" "$traffic_models_dir/tokens"
for file in catk_v120/config.yaml catk_v120/latest.ckpt \
  tokens/cabs_tc_map_vocab_c2048_t1000.pkl tokens/cabs_tc_base_agent_vocab_c1024.pkl; do
  curl --fail --location "$traffic_models_url/$file" --output "$traffic_models_dir/$file"
done

Validate their byte count and SHA256 against the Git LFS pointers bundled in the NuRec image:

docker compose run --rm -T --entrypoint python nurec-experiment - <<'PYTHON'
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib

source = Path("/opt/alpasim/data/trafficsim-models")
weights = Path("models/alpasim-trafficsim")
for relative in (
    "catk_v120/config.yaml", "catk_v120/latest.ckpt",
    "tokens/cabs_tc_map_vocab_c2048_t1000.pkl",
    "tokens/cabs_tc_base_agent_vocab_c1024.pkl",
):
    pointer = dict(line.split(" ", 1) for line in (source / relative).read_text().splitlines())
    data = (weights / relative).read_bytes()
    digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    assert len(data) == int(pointer["size"]), relative
    assert digest == pointer["oid"].removeprefix("sha256:"), relative
    print(relative, len(data), digest)
PYTHON

With traffic configured, supply the weights directory to run:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml \
  --trafficsim-models models/alpasim-trafficsim

See Reactive traffic for configuration and behavior.

docs.title: Optional assets
docs.text:
PCTNet harmonization requires third_party/libcom, einops and huggingface-hub. Only avsectester:nurec includes the latter two dependencies. Initialize libcom with the same HTTPS rewrite used for the other submodules:

git -c url.https://github.com/.insteadOf=git@github.com: submodule update --init --depth 1 -- third_party/libcom

Provide local PCTNet.pth weights from Libcom pretrained models when possible. Without a local checkpoint, the harmonizer downloads weights on first use. See the harmonizer API for loading options.

SAM person-cutout preparation accepts a model ID or local model/processor directory. Run it in nurec-experiment:

docker compose run --rm --entrypoint python nurec-experiment \
  -m scripts.preparation.extract_person_cutouts --help

Existing cutouts can be deployed without SAM.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text: Use the corresponding Compose service's version command, then follow the offline checks in Tests. Simulator, renderer and model prerequisites are listed there.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Run Quickstart, then see Experiments and Configuration.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Audience: Users running their first experiment.

Outcome: Run a comparison and open its saved reports.

Prerequisites: Installation, including data and model weights.

docs.title: Run a CARLA comparison
docs.text:
Select the available CARLA server and experiment GPUs in the Compose settings described in Installation. Copy the configuration first:

cp configs/carla_phantom.yaml configs/my_carla.yaml

Edit configs/my_carla.yaml: simulator.options.client.connect_ip and simulator.options.client.connect_port select the endpoint, and avstack.options.pipeline_cfg.perception.gpu selects the perception GPU. Set runs.output to ../results/my_carla.

docker compose up -d carla-server carla-experiment
docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester run configs/my_carla.yaml

The command prepares the configured attacks, executes treatments and evaluates saved evidence. Workflow and resume behavior are described in Experiments.

docs.title: Run a NuRec comparison
docs.text:
Place NuRec 26.01 scenes under data/nurec/26.01_release and prepare the YOLOX weights listed in Installation. The supplied split.train_segments: 5 requires at least six selected approaches. Copy the configuration within configs/:

cp configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_modular_2601.yaml configs/my_stop_sign.yaml

Edit configs/my_stop_sign.yaml and set runs.output to ../results/my_stop_sign. Set NUREC_GPU in .env. simulator.options.renderer.options.endpoint selects NRE, and the top-level device selects the detector device inside the experiment container.

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run configs/my_stop_sign.yaml

The command manages NRE automatically. Service reuse and GPU options are described in the CLI reference. See Stop-sign patch for white-box attack and black-box attack configurations, and Supplied examples for the full configuration list.

docs.title: Read the reports
docs.text: Open offline_report.html and evaluation_report.html under runs.output. The output is in the mounted checkout on the host. Structured JSON/CSV and per-run evidence are described in the Output layout.

docs.title: Reuse preparation
docs.text:
Copy a configuration, then edit configs/carla_phantom_reuse.yaml to set runs.output to ../results/carla_phantom_reused:

cp configs/my_carla.yaml configs/carla_phantom_reuse.yaml

Reuse preparation with the edited copy:

docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester run \
  configs/carla_phantom_reuse.yaml --prepared results/my_carla

For NuRec, use the same command through nurec-experiment:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml --prepared RESULTS_DIRECTORY

See Saved-preparation compatibility. To continue interrupted preparation or execution, use --resume:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml --resume

docs.title: Re-evaluate saved evidence
docs.text:
Evaluation reads the saved experiment outputs:

docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester evaluate configs/my_carla.yaml
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment evaluate \
  configs/my_stop_sign.yaml

See Evaluation for metrics and comparison groups.

docs.title: Stop CARLA
docs.text:
When finished with CARLA commands, stop its services:

docker compose down

docs.text: Choose a supplied configuration, read Writing attacks, or configure a driving system.

docs.title: Implement an attack
docs.text:
Audience: Attack authors.

Outcome: Select segments, prepare artifacts and deploy actions through public interfaces.

Prerequisites: Architecture.

docs.title: What a user implements
docs.text:
Every attack has an offline phase and an online phase. Either phase can be a no-op. Keep reusable parameters on Attack and mutable per-run state on a fresh AttackRuntime.

Entry point Responsibility build_metadata(scenario) The metabuilder selects AttackSegment records (optional with metadata.load) validate_segment(segment) Reject metadata that lacks the data or geometry the attack requires deployment_ticks(segment) Declare the deployment tick budget needed before the first capture run_offline(context) Prepare and return artifacts. The default returns None create_runtime(segment, artifacts) Create a fresh runtime for the online phase

Use Experiment workflows for preparation, execution and resume semantics. Constructor signatures, constraints and errors are in the Python API.

docs.title: Write your first attack
docs.text:
Put user implementations in your own importable package. Reference them by a full type path:

attacks:
  speed_spoof:
    type: my_project.attacks:SpeedSpoofAttack
    options:
      decision_steps: 20
      reported_speed: 0.0

A supplied attack uses the implemented-attacks layout. Keep explicit constructor parameters as attributes with the same names, or override configuration_parameters() to describe the configured inputs. Filesystem options follow Path resolution.

This example defines a selection rule and an online phase that changes model-visible speed:

from dataclasses import replace
from avsectester.attack import Attack, AttackRuntime, AVStackAttackAction
from avsectester.attack.segments import split_segments

class SpeedSpoofAttack(Attack):
    def __init__(self, decision_steps, reported_speed=0.0):
        self.decision_steps = decision_steps
        self.reported_speed = reported_speed

    def build_metadata(self, scenario):
        return split_segments(scenario.frames, lambda frame: True,
                              decision_steps=self.decision_steps)

    def create_runtime(self, segment, artifacts):
        return SpeedSpoofAttackRuntime(self.reported_speed)

class SpeedSpoofAttackRuntime(AttackRuntime):
    def __init__(self, reported_speed):
        self.reported_speed = reported_speed

    def step(self, context):
        return [AVStackAttackAction("observation", self.spoof)]

    def spoof(self, observation, context):
        context.record_output("reported_speed", self.reported_speed)
        return replace(observation, ego_speed=self.reported_speed)

The modified observation reaches the driving system while physical states remain unchanged. The Runtime reference defines the recorded inputs, commands and action receipts.

docs.title: Select segments
docs.text:
ScenarioView provides the decision timeline, frame data, semantic map and preparation services. Use record_reason() to explain rejected candidates, and session.can_start_at(position) to check start requirements before returning a segment. Placement and visibility criteria belong to the attack. The framework does not infer them from user_data.

AttackSegment contains scenario_id, start, stop and user_data. The decision interval is [start, stop), with stop as its terminal state. Store custom actor IDs, positions, ranks and other attack data in user_data, using JSON-like values and NumPy arrays for persisted metadata. Check these values in validate_segment() so user-supplied metadata follows the same attack rules. The metadata configuration controls saving and loading segments.

split_segments groups adjacent eligible decisions. The following self-contained example includes an eligible tail:

from avsectester.datasets import FrameReference
from avsectester.attack.segments import split_segments

frames = tuple(FrameReference("road", i, i, i * 0.1) for i in range(80))
segments = split_segments(frames, lambda frame: frame.position >= 5,
                          decision_steps=20, keep_tail=True)
assert [(s.start.position, s.stop.position) for s in segments] == [
    (5, 25), (25, 45), (45, 65), (65, 79)]
assert [s.decision_steps for s in segments] == [20, 20, 20, 14]

docs.title: Offline phase
docs.text:
A candidate rollout request is created from the chosen segment and deployment:

from avsectester.execution.services import CandidateRequest
from avsectester.execution.runner import RecordingPolicy

request = CandidateRequest(
    segment=segment, seed=context.seed, decision_steps=segment.decision_steps,
    environment=context.environment, recording=RecordingPolicy(),
    attack=self, artifacts=artifacts)

Set terminate_when to a predicate on each recorded StepRecord to finish a candidate early while retaining its recorded steps and normal attack cleanup.

The metabuilder is not run again after the offline phase. Use data split settings to control training, validation and execution membership.

Use Optimization tools to sample inputs, score candidates and collect offline reports.

The services available through the context provide sensor reads, rendering, component evaluations, scores and candidate rollouts. This example reads detached geometry and separates captured pixels from sensor-environment output using the shared in-memory components:

import numpy as np
from avsectester.execution.services import ClosedLoopServices, SensorRequest
from tests.fakes import MemoryDataset, MemorySimulator

dataset = MemoryDataset()
environment = {"sensors": [{"type": "GaussianNoise", "camera": "front",
                             "options": {"severity": 0.2}}]}
with ClosedLoopServices(dataset, MemorySimulator()) as services:
    scenario = services.scenario("scene", seed=7)
    with services.session(scenario.seed) as session:
        samples = [session.read_sensors(SensorRequest(
            scenario.scenario_id, frame, ("front",), environment, views=True))
            for frame in scenario.frames[1:4]]
        plain = session.read_sensors(SensorRequest("scene", scenario.frames[3], ("front",)))

optimization_samples = [
    {"image": sample.views["front"].data, "camera": sample.views["front"].camera,
     "cam_from_world": sample.views["front"].cam_from_world,
     "actors": sample.views["front"].actors, "ego": sample.views["front"].ego}
    for sample in samples]
assert len(optimization_samples) == 3 and not plain.views
assert all(sample.views["front"].native == {} for sample in samples)
assert all(sample["cam_from_world"].shape == (4, 4) for sample in optimization_samples)
assert np.any(samples[0].observation.sensor_data["front"] != optimization_samples[0]["image"])

Use session.render to evaluate deployed world or sensor actions. Use session.rollout when the objective depends on a driving response. Each candidate has its own run state. Service request records and capability checks are defined in the Python API.

docs.title: Online phase
docs.text:
The deployment tick budget is the maximum of hooks.setup_ticks + attack.deployment_ticks(segment) across all configured attacks, segments, seeds and treatments. Every treatment uses that budget. Larger budgets can make early starts fail can_start_at. A runtime must satisfy runtime.setup_ticks <= attack.deployment_ticks(segment).

A runtime's setup returns world actions. step returns the actions for a decision. stop releases its own resources. Declare snapshot reads with ResultSubscription. The context supplies snapshots and a clock, rather than a service that advances the world.

Choose WorldAttackAction for physical-world changes, SensorAttackAction for sensor-data replacement, and AVStackAttackAction for a driving-system stage value. The Runtime reference describes their application order and stage semantics. For insertion, InsertObject is a WorldAttackAction. InsertionAttackAction is a SensorAttackAction. Object coordinates use +X forward, +Y left and +Z up.

Placement tools belong to attack.insertion, not the dataset. A SensorView supplies camera geometry, actor poses and available depth for sensor composition. See Image insertion and Physical patch for the supplied deployment paths.

docs.title: Insert a world object
docs.text:
Return InsertObject from setup to include an object in the first capture. The action registers removal with the run's resources. This example needs no simulator server or model weights:

import numpy as np
from avsectester.attack import AttackRuntime
from avsectester.attack.insertion import InsertObject
from avsectester.execution.runner import ClosedLoopRunner, RunRequest
from avsectester.rendering import ObjectAsset
from tests.fakes import ConstantAVStack, MemorySimulator

texture = np.full((96, 96, 4), (180, 20, 20, 255), dtype=np.uint8)
texture[12:-12, 12:-12, :3] = (240, 240, 240)
asset = ObjectAsset.from_panel(texture, category="stop_sign", width_m=0.9,
                               mount_height_m=1.5, post_count=1)
world_from_object = np.eye(4)
world_from_object[:3, :3] = np.diag([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0])
world_from_object[:3, 3] = (8.0, 0.0, 0.0)

class PlaceSignAttackRuntime(AttackRuntime):
    def setup(self, context):
        return [InsertObject("demo_stop_sign", asset, world_from_object)]

with MemorySimulator().create_runtime() as simulator_runtime:
    log = ClosedLoopRunner().run(simulator_runtime, ConstantAVStack(),
                                RunRequest(1, attacks=(PlaceSignAttackRuntime(),)))
    assert "demo_stop_sign" in log.steps[0].physical_pre.objects
    assert not simulator_runtime.state().objects
assert log.status == "completed"

ObjectAsset uses a bottom-center local origin. Convert a map feature's reference point before placing the asset. Geometry records and asset constraints are in the Python API. This example derives a sign placement from a semantic map:

import numpy as np
from avsectester.attack import AttackRuntime
from avsectester.attack.insertion import InsertObject
from avsectester.execution.runner import ClosedLoopRunner, RecordingPolicy, RunRequest
from avsectester.geometry.poses import transform
from avsectester.maps import Lane, ScenarioMap, StopLine, TrafficControl
from avsectester.rendering import ObjectAsset
from tests.fakes import ConstantAVStack, MemoryDataset, MemorySimulator

centerline = np.array([[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [12.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
lane = Lane("approach", centerline, centerline + (0.0, 2.0, 0.0),
            centerline - (0.0, 2.0, 0.0))
face_pose = np.eye(4)
face_pose[:3, :3] = np.diag([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0])
face_pose[:3, 3] = (8.0, 0.0, 2.0)
control = TrafficControl("stop", "stop_sign", "demo_stop_sign", face_pose,
                         (0.02, 0.9, 0.9), pose_reference="face_center",
                         lane_ids=(lane.id,), stop_line_id="stop-line")
stop_line = StopLine("stop-line", np.array([[7.0, -2.0, 0.0], [7.0, 2.0, 0.0]]),
                     native_category="STOP", kind="stop_sign",
                     lane_ids=(lane.id,), control_id=control.id)
dataset = MemoryDataset(maps={"scene": ScenarioMap(
    lanes={lane.id: lane}, traffic_controls={control.id: control},
    stop_lines={stop_line.id: stop_line})})
scenario_map = dataset.scenario_map("scene")
control = scenario_map.traffic_controls["stop"]
assert control.pose_reference == "face_center"
center = control.pose[:3, 3]
candidates = []
for lane_id in control.lane_ids:  # the nearest centerline point over every governed lane
    centerline = scenario_map.lanes[lane_id].centerline
    starts, vectors = centerline[:-1], np.diff(centerline, axis=0)
    fraction = np.clip(np.sum((center - starts) * vectors, axis=1)
                       / np.sum(vectors * vectors, axis=1), 0.0, 1.0)
    candidates.append(starts + fraction[:, None] * vectors)
points = np.concatenate(candidates)
ground_z = points[np.argmin(np.linalg.norm(points - center, axis=1))][2]
c = control.pose[2, 3] - ground_z
width = control.extent[1]
texture = np.full((96, 96, 4), (180, 20, 20, 255), dtype=np.uint8)
texture[12:-12, 12:-12, :3] = (240, 240, 240)
# The face height follows the texture aspect ratio, which may differ from the mapped box.
face_height = width * texture.shape[0] / texture.shape[1]
asset = ObjectAsset.from_panel(texture, category="stop_sign", width_m=width,
                               mount_height_m=c - face_height / 2, post_count=1)
offset = np.eye(4)
offset[2, 3] = -c
world_from_object = control.pose @ offset
face_corners = transform(world_from_object, asset.surfaces[-1].corners)
post_corners = transform(world_from_object, asset.surfaces[0].corners)
np.testing.assert_allclose(face_corners.mean(axis=0), control.pose[:3, 3])
np.testing.assert_allclose(post_corners[:, 2].min(), ground_z)

class PlaceSignAttackRuntime(AttackRuntime):
    def setup(self, context):
        return [InsertObject("demo_stop_sign", asset, world_from_object)]

with MemorySimulator().create_runtime() as simulator_runtime:
    start = dataset.scenario_start("scene", dataset.frames("scene")[0])
    simulator_runtime.reset(start)
    clean = simulator_runtime.observe().sensor_data["front"].copy()
    log = ClosedLoopRunner().run(simulator_runtime, ConstantAVStack(),
        RunRequest(1, start=start, attacks=(PlaceSignAttackRuntime(),),
                   recording=RecordingPolicy(sensor_ids=("front",), representations=("raw",))))
    record = log.steps[0]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(record.physical_pre.objects["demo_stop_sign"].pose,
                               world_from_object)
    assert np.any(record.raw_observation.sensor_data["front"] != clean)
    assert record.object_visibility["demo_stop_sign"]["front"].visible_pixels > 0
    assert not simulator_runtime.state().objects
assert log.status == "completed"

World insertion, visibility, depth, occlusion and non-camera limitations are defined by the Simulator guide. Pass a harmonizer through the placed object or insertion action. Optimization tools explains the differentiable composition path.

docs.title: Datasets and semantic maps
docs.text:
Audience: Attack and dataset authors.

Outcome: Read scene timelines, recorded states and semantic maps.

Prerequisites: Architecture.

docs.title: Dataset interface
docs.text:
A Dataset exposes recorded records or CARLA recipes. It never owns a simulator. Its public methods list scenarios and frames, read frame data, expose native source records and construct a ScenarioStart for a chosen frame. Mutable return values are independent of cached dataset reads. See the Dataset interface for signatures and validation rules.

ScenarioStart carries scenario_id, the selected frame, kind and payload, the complete recorded_ego sequence and scenario_map. The dataset creates this simulator-independent start record.

Record Purpose ScenarioDescriptor Stable scene identity and provider payload FrameReference Scenario identity, timeline position, native frame ID and timestamp FrameData Recorded ego, other actors, sensor references and provenance ActorState Actor-origin pose, velocity, category, optional extent and local box transform SensorDataReference Native sensor name, payload location, timestamp and decoding metadata ScenarioStart Source payload, recorded ego timeline and semantic map used for reset Unavailable Missing evidence with an explicit reason

FrameData.actors excludes the ego. FrameData.ego contains it. Timeline position and native frame ID are distinct. A window of N decisions needs N+1 supported frame references, including its terminal state.

ActorState.pose is world-from-actor, while box_center and box_rotation describe the local box center and orientation. box_transform() returns world-from-box-center without changing the actor origin. Velocity uses world-frame meters per second. Extent is full length, width and height in meters. An unknown extent is None, distinct from known zero dimensions. Pose-only operations accept unknown extent. Attached placement and cuboid occlusion require known dimensions. See record constraints.

CARLA recipes have no recorded ego timeline. Map records are shared as read-only data. Start payloads are independent copies.

docs.title: CARLA recipes
docs.text:
CarlaDataset holds named CarlaRecipe records. Each recipe supplies actor spawns and prescribed motion: constant control, per-decision controls or an ActorState trajectory. A recipe includes its terminal state. Prescribed execution follows Simulators.

CARLA frame data is generated by experiment preparation and cached separately. CarlaDataset returns Unavailable for that generated evidence. See CARLA recipe types and the preparation workflow.

docs.title: NuRec recordings
docs.text:
NuRecDataset reads the archives selected by dataset configuration. Recursive dataroot discovery uses path order. An explicit usdz_paths list supplies the archives directly. Scenario identities are native clip identifiers rather than filesystem paths.

Decision frames use the configured time_step. Ego and actor poses interpolate within recording support and do not extrapolate. An actor outside its recorded support is absent. Camera timestamps describe recorded image frames and are distinct from the decision timeline. Use camera_timestamps when aligning video labels and camera_geometry for the optical model and rig-from-camera transform.

FrameData.sensor_references retains the native camera_id. Model-visible name changes belong to the simulator's camera_aliases, not the dataset. Dataset camera and trajectory methods take scenario_id. Their signatures and calibration constraints are in the NuRec API.

The public read_scene_mesh function reads world-coordinate mesh vertices and triangle faces without selecting a camera. NuRecDataset.scene_mesh and the simulator share that reader. Depth and ground contact are simulator behavior.

docs.title: nuScenes recordings
docs.text:
NuScenesDataset exposes scene tokens, recorded keyframe timelines and stable actor instance IDs. It retains annotated categories and full extents. Sensor references use the configured native camera name, such as CAM_FRONT.

RecordedReplaySimulator reads these references. Driving commands do not change recorded motion. Configure its model-visible sensor names through simulator aliases. The nuScenes API defines source options.

docs.title: Semantic maps
docs.text:
Dataset.scenario_map returns ScenarioMap or an Unavailable value with a reason. The base implementation provides no map. ScenarioView.scenario_map exposes it during selection. Missing map evidence does not prevent other dataset operations. An attack decides whether it can use that scenario.

Dataset Map source NuRec Aligned clipgt geometry from the scene archive CARLA Exported OpenDRIVE through the optional CARLA client package nuScenes Not yet implemented. See nuScenes semantic maps.

Maps contain lanes, drivable polygons, road boundaries, crosswalks, intersections, controls and stop lines. Inspect unavailable_layers for missing layer evidence. An empty known layer and an unavailable layer have different meanings. Geometry uses canonical world meters and read-only arrays.

The map record formats define coordinate conventions and control pose references. The clipgt reader and OpenDRIVE reader define source associations, classification rules and alignment limits.

A custom Dataset can construct the shared map records or return Unavailable. For an OpenDRIVE source aligned with its canonical world frame, it can reuse read_opendrive. Constructor path handling follows filesystem parameter rules.

Maps are selection and evaluation evidence, not AVStack observations. An attack copies the map information needed by its online phase into segment user_data. Dynamic signal states are recorded separately in WorldSnapshot.

docs.title: Driving systems
docs.text:
Audience: Experiment authors and driving-system implementers.

Outcome: Select a supplied driving system or bind a custom system.

Prerequisites: Architecture.

docs.title: AVStack interface
docs.text:
AVStack receives an Observation and returns a Control. It declares supported command modes, stages and optional recorded-input requirements. The simulator and driving system must agree on commands and decision timing. See Configuration.

Interfaces live in avsectester.closed_loop.avstacks. Supplied implementations live below avstacks.implemented. User implementations belong in the user's package.

ObservationPipeline processes current input in this order:

  1. sensors.post hooks.
  2. localization.pre hooks and the configured localizer, when present.
  3. localization.post hooks.
  4. observation hooks.

The pipeline owns the localizer lifecycle and does not process output commands. Runtime defines the complete per-decision order and record formats.

docs.title: Recorded input history
docs.text: History acquisition and processing follow Past observations. AVStack.past_steps declares the required history and is read without constructing the model.

docs.title: avstack modular pipeline (ModularAVStack)
docs.text:
The *_modular_* stop-sign configurations use RuleBasedAVStack, described below.

ModularAVStack wraps avstack's perception, tracking, planning and control pipeline. Each run gets fresh component histories. Native models and component outputs remain avstack objects.

instrument captures selected component outputs. detections converts supported perception boxes to the true capture-time ego frame without another inference call. Model-visible localization does not change that coordinate conversion. Unsupported perception output returns None, while an empty sequence means supported perception with no detections.

NativeHook wraps explicitly registered native hook implementations. Registration modules can be listed in the hook configuration. The framework's phantom action can instead modify the declared perception stage directly. See Hooks.

docs.title: Camera forward-collision policy
docs.text:
CameraForwardCollisionAVStack uses a 2D image detector and image-box area to choose braking or throttle. Its learned model loads lazily and can be shared with bound scorers.

CameraForwardCollisionAVStack exposes its scorer through modular_driving_adapter.

This policy exposes 2D component diagnostics, not canonical 3D detections. DetectionMetrics requires a driving system that provides 3D detections. See Evaluation.

docs.title: NuRec rule-based driving system
docs.text:
RuleBasedAVStack composes a YOLOXDetector, StopSignTracker and StopSignPlanner. Its processing chain is detection, known-size ranging, bearing EKF tracking and trajectory planning. YOLOXDetector is a general COCO detector. The stack uses its stop sign detections. It requires the selected camera's CameraCalibration and a planar ego state.

The cruise reference v0 is cruise_speed_mps, or the speed at reset bounded below by min_cruise_speed_mps when cruise speed is omitted. The tracker never deletes tracks, adds no process noise, and wraps bearing residuals across ±π. Stop signs facing another direction can still trigger a stop if they pass the route filters. provides_detections=False makes this stack incompatible with DetectionMetrics.

The stack selects stop-sign boxes and confidence. Ranging uses the angular height of a box and the assumed sign height, then transforms the point from optical-camera coordinates into rig coordinates. Distance error scales with error in the assumed physical sign size.

The tracker stores stationary signs in world coordinates. Range and bearing uncertainty determine association. Bearing-only EKF updates refine associated tracks. The planner identifies a target and served signs by track ID.

The planner projects tracks onto the navigation route, filters signs outside its forward/lateral range, and places the stop target before a relevant sign. With no route it uses a straight route. Cruise acceleration is the IDM free-road term, a_max * (1 - (v / v0) ** delta). Here a_max is max_acceleration_mps2 and delta is acceleration_exponent.

For a stop target at remaining route distance d, the required deceleration is v² / (2d). Reaching comfortable_deceleration_mps2 latches braking. The planner then follows that required deceleration and does not return to cruise for the same target. Acceleration is limited by the configured acceleration/deceleration bounds. Late detection can require more braking than available and can produce a stop beyond the target.

After the speed and position criteria are met, the planner holds its stop for the configured duration, marks that track served, and resumes cruise. Reset clears tracking and planning state. The Python API lists defaults, parameter meanings and errors.

The component log records boxes, estimated positions, tracks with covariance summaries, target distance, state and braking. acceleration_mps2 and planned_speed_mps describe the first planned trajectory step. A controller tracks the whole forecast and can slow the vehicle while that planned first-step acceleration is positive.

This system handles stop signs only. It follows the navigation centerline without perceiving other vehicles or obstacles. Recorded non-reactive traffic can hit ego from behind. Intruding vehicles can also overlap its path. DrivingMetrics.collision records those physical overlaps.

docs.title: Alpamayo
docs.text:
AlpamayoAVStack uses AlpaSim's policy interface to turn camera input, ego pose history, speed, acceleration and navigation into a rig-frame trajectory. Navigation comes from Observation.route, which the simulator generates as route intent. It is independent of the executed future path. See Navigation. By default it uses the four cameras of AlpaSim's Alpamayo 1.5 driver: front wide, front tele and both cross cameras. The renderer must provide every listed camera.

Component logs contain policy, command, route_waypoints, navigation_command, navigation_note, history_pose_count and selected_image_times. Without a route, the navigation command falls back to STRAIGHT.

Camera images and pose history must match the declared decision timeline. History validation rejects missing or inconsistent observations. The stack transforms policy outputs into the common trajectory command format. Native policy output, including optional reasoning, remains available through component logging.

docs.title: Loading and sharing the model
docs.text: Local checkpoint loading happens lazily. Injecting a model allows the caller to supply an already-constructed policy. Closing releases a model loaded by the stack. An injected model is borrowed and is not closed. Closing the stack is terminal and idempotent. Checkpoint locations and installation are specified in Installation.

docs.title: Component logging interface
docs.text: component_log returns optional component outputs for the most recent decision. The runner snapshots them independently. detections returns canonical 3D detections or None when unsupported. The Runtime reference describes field layout and serialization.

docs.title: Components and scorers for offline work
docs.text:
A DrivingAdapter binds reusable component/scorer declarations to a factory that creates fresh driving systems. Discovery reads static declarations and configured options without constructing a stack or loading model weights. Constructor injection belongs to Configuration.

rule_based_driving_adapter exposes rule_based.detection_confidence. Its sensor_id comes from the configured camera_id or the stack default, and decision_threshold comes from detector.score_threshold. Missing detector configuration or a detector other than YOLOXDetector raises ValueError. The scorer accepts any COCO class name as target.label.

Binding Purpose modular_driving_adapter Modular perception components and bound image scorers rule_based_driving_adapter The rule-based driver's detection-confidence scorer alpamayo_driving_adapter Policy prediction from current and preceding observations

The Alpamayo binding declares 15 preceding decisions when a factory has no AVStack type metadata.

Scorer callbacks have signature (avstack, images, targets) and return one score per input. Built-in descriptors name the input images and output scores. output_shape=() describes one input's scalar score. Differentiable scorers declare "BCHW float tensor [0,1]" and differentiable_inputs=("images",). Inference scorers declare "list of HWC RGB uint8". Image and target batch lengths must agree.

Scorers also declare objective direction, camera and decision threshold where applicable. A white-box attack can use the same detector as the driving system through its scorer binding. See Optimization.

docs.title: Use a custom driving system
docs.text:
Implement AVStack in a user package and reference it as type: my_project.driving:CustomAVStack. Declare required history, compatible command modes and optional decision timing. A separate binding factory exposes components or scorers when the experiment needs them.

A minimal actuator policy needs no simulator connection:

from avsectester.closed_loop.avstacks import AVStack
from avsectester.data_types import Control, Observation


class CruiseStack(AVStack):
    command_modes = frozenset({"actuator"})

    def __call__(self, observation):
        return Control(throttle=0.2)


stack = CruiseStack()
observation = Observation(0.0, 0)
stack.reset(observation)
assert stack(observation).throttle == 0.2
stack.close()
