docs.title: Experiment environments
docs.text:
Audience: Experiment authors studying world or sensor conditions.

Outcome: Configure environmental treatments and explicit selection conditions.

Prerequisites: Configuration.

docs.title: Experiment environment
docs.text:
An environment separates world settings, applied by the simulator at reset, from sensor corruptions, applied to captured model inputs. The merge order is runs.environment, the enabled Attack.environment and the treatment environment. World mappings merge recursively. An explicitly provided sensor list replaces the preceding list.

runs:
  environment:
    sensors:
      - {type: GaussianNoise, options: {severity: 0.2}, camera: front}
  treatments:
    - {name: clean}
    - name: heavy_noise
      environment:
        sensors:
          - {type: GaussianNoise, options: {severity: 0.7}, camera: front}

The YAML keys and defaults are defined in environment configuration.

docs.title: Selection and the offline phase
docs.text:
Metabuilders do not inherit the experiment environment. Selection requests must supply any desired environment explicitly. OfflineContext.environment merges runs.environment with the attack's environment. Pass it to sensor reads, renders or candidate rollouts when those conditions are required.

Changing an environment does not reselect segments. The attack owns eligibility decisions. See selection and metadata.

docs.title: Sensor processing
docs.text:
Sensor corruptions change model-visible captures without changing physical state. The runtime sequence places them between sensor attack actions and the observation pipeline.

Camera selection follows Environment configuration.

Camera transport preserves RGB uint8. Non-camera writes preserve the payload representation and dtype. Neither path infers sensor type from array shape. See data transport.

docs.title: Supplied corruptions
docs.text:
Built-in image corruptions approximate weather, lighting and sensor effects in image space. Fog does not integrate metric scene depth, and procedural rain is not physical rainfall. They are separate from native world settings. The corruption API lists the classes and parameters.

This complete configuration uses the repository's memory components and a built-in corruption. It loads without a simulator service, model weights or GPU.

dataset: {type: "tests.fakes:MemoryDataset"}
simulator: {type: "tests.fakes:MemorySimulator"}
avstack: {type: "tests.fakes:ConstantAVStack"}
attacks:
  probe: {type: "tests.fakes:MinimalAttack"}
runs:
  environment:
    sensors:
      - type: GaussianNoise
        options: {severity: 0.2}
        camera: front

AlbumentationsCorruption selects an Albumentations transform through its transform option and requires the augment extra. It uses the same sensor-environment mechanism. See constructor options.

docs.title: Custom sensor corruptions
docs.text:
Implement apply(rgb, rng), or a callable with that signature, returning uint8 RGB with the same shape. Select it with a constructor path such as my_project.corruptions:DimImage. Filesystem constructor parameters follow path resolution.

import numpy as np

class DimImage:
    def __init__(self, factor=0.8):
        self.factor = factor

    def apply(self, rgb, rng):
        return np.clip(rgb.astype(float) * self.factor, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

image = np.full((4, 5, 3), 100, dtype=np.uint8)
assert DimImage().apply(image, np.random.default_rng(0))[0, 0, 0] == 80

docs.title: Native world settings
docs.text:
World-setting support and keys are defined in Configuration.

Conditions changed by a world attack action during execution are recorded as actions, rather than as static environment settings. Native simulator behavior is described in Simulators.

Not yet implemented. Reference evaluations that train and test artifacts under different conditions. See Environment transfer.

docs.title: Randomness
docs.text: Sensor corruptions use a fresh NumPy generator keyed by (run_seed, absolute_dataset_position, corruption_index). Past and current captures at the same dataset position therefore use the same corruption randomness. Hooks share a run-scoped NumPy generator initialized from the hook seed. Registration and execution order determine its consumption. Shared callback handlers retain their declared lifecycle.

docs.title: Evaluate experiments
docs.text:
Audience: Researchers analyzing recorded experiments.

Outcome: Measure treatments and comparison groups without running a simulator.

Prerequisites: Experiments.

docs.title: Saved logs are the input
docs.text:
Evaluation reads saved preparation, maps and RunLog records after execution. It does not read dataset frames, load deployment artifacts or run model inference. Missing evidence cannot be reconstructed. Failed or unreadable runs keep their failure status. Unavailable measurements carry reasons rather than becoming zero.

ExperimentResult.load restores the saved evidence. Report rebuilding and skipped-run notices follow the CLI evaluate command.

docs.title: Comparison groups
docs.text:
Every unattacked treatment runs once per unit and seed. An attacked treatment runs only in units selected by its attack. All applicable treatments in a group are compared pairwise.

The architecture terms define units and comparison groups. RunGroup retains all supplied logs in their order, including failed, cancelled and incomplete logs, plus optional errors, part, treatment attacks and a scenario map.

evaluate_groups passes only completed logs to the ComparisonGroup supplied to each metric. All treatment pairs are considered in supplied order. For treatments A then B, single-run metric differences are B − A. Boolean values are treated as 0 or 1. An unfinished pair or unavailable value produces a reason, not a zero difference.

PairMetric receives a TreatmentPair directly. TrajectoryDeviation measures symmetric trajectory distance. StopImpact evaluates both A-to-B and B-to-A stopping effects. These pair measurements do not receive another difference operation.

docs.title: Built-in metrics
docs.text:
Metric Measurements DrivingMetrics Physical speed, executed actuator braking, stopping, actor distance and geometric collision TrajectoryDeviation Ego-position deviation at matched decision indices DetectionMetrics Thresholded detection matching, precision, recall and F1 StopImpact Stopping and braking comparisons in both directions StopLineMetrics Physical stopping, crossing and signed distance relative to the selected map stop line ReasoningPhraseRate Case-insensitive phrase mentions in recorded reasoning text

The metric API defines constructor parameters and unavailable conditions. The default set and YAML validation are described in evaluation configuration.

DrivingMetrics uses executed actuator commands for brake_steps. Trajectory commands do not provide that evidence. Collision is bird's-eye oriented-box overlap, not a native collision-sensor event. TrajectoryDeviation compares true ego positions at equal decision indices, without time or route alignment.

Not yet implemented. Matched-window driving-impact measures with prior-motion and duration requirements. See Driving-impact metrics.

DetectionMetrics matches detections to true actors in the capture-time ego frame, using sensor mounting geometry independently of model localization. Its range filtering is horizontal. Category matching follows category_map when configured. The thresholded detections do not define TN or AP/mAP.

StopLineMetrics uses segment.user_data["stop_line_id"] to identify a stop line in the saved map and assumes the run starts before it. It uses the initial physical state and each decision's physical result. Distances are horizontal and positive before the first crossing, then negative. Crossing speed is interpolated between adjacent samples. Three distances distinguish stopping and physical braking:

  • distance_to_line_at_stop uses the first sample below stop_speed, also used by time_to_stop. It is unavailable if the ego never stops.
  • distance_to_line_at_min_speed uses the first minimum-speed sample before crossing, or the whole run when no crossing occurs.
  • distance_to_line_at_brake_onset uses the start of the first adjacent-sample interval whose speed decrease divided by elapsed time reaches brake_deceleration_mps2. It is unavailable with fewer than two samples or no qualifying interval.

Brake onset uses physical speed rather than an actuator command. A stop after crossing has negative distance_to_line_at_stop. Missing line, map or physical evidence produces unavailable measurements. Metric.describe supplies field definitions to the reports. The metric API defines parameter constraints.

ReasoningPhraseRate reads native component attributes or mapping fields. Its rate uses all decisions as the denominator and is unavailable if any decision lacks text.

docs.title: Reports and statistics
docs.text:
Boolean values display as yes or no, floats with four decimal places, and unavailable or nonfinite values as an em dash (—). Numeric summaries use mean ± std and n = k, omitting the standard deviation for one observation. Boolean summaries show the true fraction and x of K groups. HTML pages contain inline styling without scripts or external resources. Saved images and CSV files are linked relative to the page. JSON and CSV retain full precision.

Treatment summaries group measurements by part and treatment. Pair summaries group by part and treatment pair. Numeric summaries use the mean and population standard deviation (ddof=0), with a separate available-group count for each field. Boolean summaries use the true fraction. Unavailable values are excluded from that field's denominator.

Paired differences are computed inside each group before aggregation. PairMetric measurements are summarized separately. Statistics do not infer an attack-success label. See the example interpretation rule.

The HTML report presents experiment setup, metric definitions, run status, per-part results, paired differences and group details. Group details retain unavailable reasons and saved plots. The command line shows per-part metric tables, notes and errors. Paired tables are in the HTML and structured report. format_summary returns a string, so Python callers print it explicitly.

Output locations follow the CLI reference. Offline phase results are separate. Optimization describes their report interface.

Saved metric specifications include type, options, label, kind, summary and fields.

docs.title: Custom metrics
docs.text:
Metric.evaluate returns a mapping from treatment names to scalar field mappings. Scalars can be numbers, booleans or UnavailableMetricValue with a reason and a number/boolean type. PairMetric instead returns one field mapping for its TreatmentPair. MetricScalar is a scalar or unavailable value. FieldMeasurements maps field names to those values, and TreatmentMeasurements maps treatment names to field mappings. Return missing evidence explicitly rather than keeping mutable per-run state. See the metric types.

The default Metric.describe uses the first paragraph of the class docstring as its summary and supplies no field descriptions.

Describe each field's meaning, unit and unavailable conditions through Metric.describe. Reports retain the complete metric label, so dotted field names remain attached to the correct metric. Description failures are recorded as metric errors. Absent descriptions display "No description provided".

from avsectester.evaluation import Metric, MetricDescription, MetricField

class DecisionCount(Metric):
    def describe(self):
        return MetricDescription(
            "Number of recorded decisions in a run.",
            {"decision_count": MetricField("Decisions saved in the run log.", "decision steps")},
        )

    def evaluate(self, group):
        return {name: {"decision_count": len(log.steps)}
                for name, log in group.runs.items()}

Configure the class with a path such as my_project.metrics:DecisionCount. A metric reads recorded evidence and does not require simulator startup, dataset access or model inference.

docs.title: Visualize saved observations
docs.text:
Retain the needed sensor payloads before execution using recording configuration. camera_view and lidar_bev read saved inputs. labels_view projects recorded true actors, while detections_view projects recorded detections. sensor_view reconstructs only logged geometry.

The following example requires retained camera payloads in a saved run:

from avsectester.runlog import RunLog
from avsectester.evaluation.visualization import camera_view, record_run, save_gif

log = RunLog.read("results/experiment/runs/segment-00000/seed-0/clean")
record_run(log, "export/frames", visualize=camera_view)
save_gif(log, "export/drive.gif", fps=5)

record_run exports frames, filmstrip creates a grid and save_sequence exports images and animation. These functions consume saved records and do not drive a world. Missing input produces no view. Overlays use only the recorded camera geometry. See the visualization API for constraints.

docs.title: Evaluate existing RunLog objects
docs.text:
Use RunGroup and evaluate_groups directly when logs are already in memory. They require neither Experiment nor a dataset. Save the returned report when persistent files are needed.

import numpy as np
from avsectester.attack import AttackSegment
from avsectester.datasets import FrameReference
from avsectester.data_types import ActorState, Control, WorldSnapshot
from avsectester.evaluation import DrivingMetrics, RunGroup, evaluate_groups
from avsectester.runlog import RunLog, StepRecord

ego = ActorState(np.eye(4), (1, 0, 0), "vehicle", (4, 2, 1.5))
state = WorldSnapshot(0.1, 1, ego_speed=1.0, ego=ego)
log = RunLog(steps=[StepRecord(0, physical_pre=state, physical_post=state,
                             executed_command=Control())], status="completed")
start = FrameReference("road", 0, 0, 0.0)
stop = FrameReference("road", 1, 1, 0.1)
group = RunGroup(0, AttackSegment("road", start, stop), 0, {"clean": log},
                 treatment_attacks={"clean": None})
report = evaluate_groups((group,), (DrivingMetrics(),), notes=("Existing in-memory log",))
assert len(report.groups) == 1
assert report.notes == ["Existing in-memory log"]
print(report.format_summary())

docs.title: Experiments
docs.text:
Audience: Experiment authors.

Outcome: Prepare artifacts, execute treatments and resume saved work.

Prerequisites: Architecture.

docs.title: Prepare and execute attacks
docs.text:
Experiment accepts a typed configuration, mapping or YAML path. prepare selects or loads segments and runs each configured attack's offline phase. execute runs the selected treatment groups. evaluate measures their recorded evidence. PreparedExperiment contains metadata, units, artifacts and offline reports, without live simulator or AVStack history.

This complete example uses the repository's memory components and a temporary output directory. It needs no simulator service, model weights or GPU.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from avsectester.experiment import Experiment, evaluate, load_configuration

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    configuration = load_configuration({
        "dataset": {"type": "tests.fakes:MemoryDataset"},
        "simulator": {"type": "tests.fakes:MemorySimulator"},
        "avstack": {"type": "tests.fakes:ConstantAVStack"},
        "attacks": {"probe": {"type": "tests.fakes:MinimalAttack"}},
        "runs": {"output": str(Path(directory) / "run")},
    })
    Experiment.validate(configuration)
    prepared = Experiment.prepare(configuration)
    result = Experiment.execute(prepared)
    report = evaluate(result, configuration)
    assert not result.failures
    assert not report.metric_errors
    print(report.format_summary())

See automatic local services for CLI and Python use.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
Preparation selects every attack before running any offline phase. It checks selected boundaries, applies the common deployment tick budget and builds shared segment units. A supplied metadata file replaces selection. Attack.validate_segment checks selected and loaded segments.

After build_metadata returns, preparation drops segments that fail can_start_at or whose validate_start raises UnsupportedStartError. The experiment-wide budget recheck drops segments that then fail can_start_at. Each drop records its reason. See deployment tick budgets.

Preparation uses the first configured run seed and reuses its metadata for all execution seeds. Its environment rules are defined in Environments: an offline phase receives the merged experiment and attack environment, while selection requests an environment explicitly.

PreparedExperiment retains all units, including those excluded from execution. Unit identity, the split schema and deterministic allocation are defined in Data split.

Not yet implemented. Sharing unattacked runs across units with different user_data. See shared runs across different user data.

docs.title: Input validation
docs.text:
validate and prepare reject existing preparation output without resume=True. Environment checks run for fresh and resumed preparations. A fresh loaded metadata file is validated once per call before offline work.

Experiment.validate checks inputs that can be checked without a SimulatorRuntime or service connection. Loaded metadata follows Save and reuse selected metadata.

For resume with saved preparation or progress, validation checks frames and compatibility, skipping eligibility and validate_start. The CLI skips this preflight when it has already loaded preparation for --prepared or a completed preparation resume. CLI exit codes distinguish input failures from execution failures.

docs.title: Treatments and common origins
docs.text:
The architecture defines units and comparison groups. Each enabled treatment starts from the group's common origin. Membership follows Evaluation. The same configured hooks apply to every treatment.

Execution follows the deployment tick budget. Unattacked runs do not create an AttackRuntime. Each run creates fresh simulator and AVStack state, with cleanup on success, failure or interruption. The treatment schema defines how to enable attacks and environment overrides.

docs.title: Results and failures
docs.text: ExperimentResult.runs holds every treatment result. failures lists failed or incomplete runs. selection_errors lists selection errors. The runs.strict setting raises the first error. See Run settings.

docs.title: Save and reuse selected metadata
docs.text:
Loading validates dataset type, scenario and frame membership, decision windows, each attack's validate_segment, the shared deployment tick budget and simulator start requirements. An invalid segment fails with its index and reason.

Metadata files contain segments, independently of offline artifacts or run results. Use metadata.save to export all units after selection and deployment checks, before the offline phases. Existing identical content is accepted. Different content is an error.

Use metadata.load to reuse those segments with other attack settings or driving systems. Every attack receives the same supplied segments, selection is skipped and split still applies. The offline phases run for the configured attacks. Loading segments does not reuse their artifacts.

Python callers can generate segments with their own criteria using save_metadata and load_metadata. The file schema, duplicate checks, path rules and content-hash compatibility are defined in Metadata. Resuming preparation and reusing a prepared experiment do not perform selection or write metadata.save again.

docs.title: Save and reload preparation
docs.text:
Preparation checkpoints selected metadata and units before the offline phases. Each completed phase saves its artifacts and report before its name is marked complete. The complete prepared manifest is written after every configured attack has finished.

PreparedExperiment.save and load persist and restore artifacts together with metadata and reports. Loading requires an explicit compatible configuration, does not repeat selection and does not run the offline phases. Only load trusted preparation files. Artifact encoding is controlled by the attack. See compatibility rules and the preparation API.

docs.title: Resume interrupted work
docs.text:
Prepare with resume=True to reuse saved selection and completed offline phases. Execute with resume=True to retain completed runs whose expected metadata matches. Missing, failed or mismatched runs are retried individually. An already complete group needs no new initialization.

Execution resume compares attack_name, segment_index, part, the complete segment, treatment, seed, environment, decision_steps, selected_decision_steps and deployment_ticks.

An interrupted offline phase leaves progress and a partial failed report. Resuming archives that attack's report directory before restarting its offline phase. The CLI resume workflow defines command options and output handling. Offline reports explains phase output.

docs.title: Saved maps
docs.text:
Execution reads each selected scene's semantic map once and retains it in ExperimentResult.scenario_maps, including Unavailable with its reason. Persistent results save those maps with the run evidence. ExperimentResult.load restores them for ComparisonGroup.scenario_map. Evaluation does not call a dataset to fill in missing maps.

A saved result can therefore be evaluated without its dataset or metadata file. Configuration compatibility still applies. See saved preparation compatibility. The CLI output layout defines saved file locations.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: Keep the configuration, selected metadata, artifacts and RunLog manifests together. Fresh runtime and hook state isolate treatments. A common seed does not guarantee bitwise-identical native simulator or model kernels. Sensor noise uses the environment seed rules.

docs.title: Environment-only robustness experiments
docs.text:
Use a selection-only Attack and configure treatments with environment overrides. Its offline and online phases may both be empty operations:

from avsectester.attack import Attack
from avsectester.attack.segments import split_segments

class SelectionOnlyAttack(Attack):
    def __init__(self, decision_steps):
        self.decision_steps = decision_steps

    def build_metadata(self, scenario):
        return split_segments(scenario.frames, lambda frame: True,
                              decision_steps=self.decision_steps)

See Environments for merge rules and supported conditions.

docs.title: Optimize attack artifacts
docs.text:
Audience: Attack authors implementing an offline objective.

Outcome: Reuse scoring, rendering and optimization tools, and report prepared artifacts.

Prerequisites: Attacks.

docs.title: Optimization interfaces
docs.text:
An attack supplies its sample selection, perturbation and objective. Algorithms do not choose scenes, hosts or placement rules.

Interface Responsibility DataSource Map-style dataset: __len__ and __getitem__ provide AdversarialSample records Perturbation Initialize, apply, project, export and measure the smoothness of a candidate Scorer target_scores(images, targets) returns one score per input OptimizationObjective Convert scores into losses GradientOptimizer Run the algorithm and return OptimizationResult

HideObject minimizes a score. SpoofObject maximizes it. HideBelowThreshold minimizes only the part of a score above a decision threshold minus a margin, for targets where one detection decides the outcome. Objectives operate elementwise on score batches. Scores can be detector confidence or a physical quantity such as distance. An optional monitor(index, delta) observes the initial variable at index 0, then each completed PGD epoch or NES step. PGD requires a differentiable score, while NES uses score queries. PGD's tv_weight weights Perturbation.smoothness, which defaults to total variation of the whole variable. A perturbation that realizes only part of it overrides the method. A SessionScorer connects either path to a declared DrivingAdapter binding. Driving-system bindings describes model integration. The Python API lists signatures and optimizer constraints.

This self-contained example uses a local scorer and needs no model weights:

import torch
from avsectester.attack.optimization import (
    AdversarialSample, DataSource, HideObject, LinfImage, PGD, Scorer,
)
from avsectester.data_types import TargetSpec

class FixedImageSource(DataSource):
    def __len__(self):
        return 1

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        if index != 0:
            raise IndexError(index)
        return AdversarialSample(torch.full((3, 8, 8), 0.5), TargetSpec((0, 0, 8, 8)))

class MeanIntensityScorer(Scorer):
    def target_scores(self, images, targets):
        if len(images) != len(targets):
            raise ValueError("Image and target batch lengths must match")
        return images.mean(dim=(1, 2, 3))

perturbation = LinfImage(epsilon=0.1, image_hw=(8, 8), device="cpu")
result = PGD(epochs=2, batch_size=1, step_size=0.01).run(
    FixedImageSource(), perturbation, MeanIntensityScorer(), HideObject())
assert result.delta.shape == (3, 8, 8)
assert torch.max(torch.abs(result.delta)).item() <= 0.1

LinfImage applies a bounded additive image change. PatchPerturbation renders texture colors using the geometry supplied in each sample. The sample's target region belongs to the objective. It is independent of the placement rule.

PGD shuffles samples using seed and retains the final smaller batch. Images in one batch must have equal dimensions. Random augmentations are redrawn in DataSource.__getitem__. OptimizationResult.history records each epoch's mean sample objective, excluding TV.

NES uses steps because it optimizes one seeded dataset sample rather than traversing the dataset. It scores candidate perturbations in groups of at most batch_size per query.

docs.title: Use a driving-system scorer
docs.text:
Create a session inside the offline phase, select a declared scorer, and keep that session open for calibration, updates and evaluation:

from avsectester.attack.optimization import HideObject, PGD, SessionScorer

# Requires OfflineContext context, a user DataSource and a Perturbation.
with context.services.session(context.seed) as session:
    scorer = SessionScorer(session, "rule_based.detection_confidence", require_grad=True,
                           input_format="BCHW float tensor [0,1]", device="cpu")
    result = PGD(epochs=10, batch_size=4).run(source, perturbation, scorer, HideObject())

Scorer declarations follow Driving-system bindings. Use candidate rollouts when the score depends on a planned trajectory or physical response.

docs.title: Optimize a world object's texture
docs.text:
A captured SensorView.composition retains the background and the composition plan used for that capture. Reuse its plan when optimizing colors. In geometry occlusion mode, a clean view can also build a plan through composite_plan. The Simulator guide describes that capability.

Differentiable harmonizers use the same floating-point computation during optimization and deployment, followed by uint8 rounding for deployment. This example checks that equivalence and backpropagates through ExposureHarmonizer:

import numpy as np
import torch

from avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.base import SensorView
from avsectester.data_types import ActorState
from avsectester.geometry.cameras import BODY_FROM_OPTICAL, PinholeCamera
from avsectester.geometry.poses import make_pose, rotation_matrix
from avsectester.rendering import ExposureHarmonizer, ObjectAsset, PlacedObject

# In an attack, use a clean ClosedLoopSession.render(...).view instead of this synthetic view.
camera = PinholeCamera(np.array([[300., 0., 160.], [0., 300., 120.], [0., 0., 1.]]), 320, 240)
view = SensorView("front", np.full((240, 320, 3), 90, np.uint8), camera,
                  np.linalg.inv(BODY_FROM_OPTICAL), {}, ActorState(np.eye(4)), 0.0, 0)
face = np.full((64, 64, 4), 255, np.uint8)
asset = ObjectAsset.from_panel(face, category="sign", width_m=0.9, mount_height_m=1.0)
sign = PlacedObject(
    "sign", asset, make_pose(rotation_matrix([0., 0., 180.]), [8., 0., -1.5]),
    harmonizer=ExposureHarmonizer(reference="under", gain_range=(0.5, 0.5)),
)

plan = view.composite_plan([sign])
colors = (torch.as_tensor(face[..., :3]).permute(2, 0, 1).float() / 255).requires_grad_()
background = torch.as_tensor(view.data).permute(2, 0, 1).float() / 255
image = plan.composite(background, {("sign", 0): colors})
deployed = plan.apply(view.data).image
rounded = image.detach().permute(1, 2, 0).mul(255).round().to(torch.uint8).numpy()
np.testing.assert_array_equal(deployed, rounded)
image.mean().backward()
assert colors.grad.abs().sum() > 0

Keep the asset's alpha when exporting colors. A surface's nominal_texture provides an unchanged appearance reference when scene statistics should not depend on the optimized texture. Harmonizer formulas, parameters and non-differentiable restrictions are described in the rendering API.

docs.title: Offline reports
docs.text:
report.json contains status, values, series, tables and images. Values retain their unit and description. Series retain coordinates, axis labels, units and description. Tables retain rows, column descriptions and CSV filenames. Images retain descriptions and PNG filenames. CSV column order is the union of row keys in first-appearance order. Auxiliary files live below files/.

The offline HTML page expands tables with at most 20 rows and eight columns. Larger tables are collapsible.

context.report collects measurements independently of returned artifacts. Each setter replaces an item with the same name and kind. Include units, descriptions and table-column explanations so the saved report is understandable without opening the implementation:

report = context.report
report.set_value("training_segments", len(context.metadata), unit="segments",
                 description="Segments used by this offline phase.")
report.set_series("confidence", objective_history, x_label="iteration",
                  y_label="Mean confidence", y_unit="ratio (0–1)",
                  description="Confidence measured before each update.")
report.set_table(
    "samples", [{"frame": 12, "distance_m": 20.0}],
    description="Captured training frames.",
    columns={"frame": "Recorded frame index.", "distance_m": "Distance to the line (m)."},
)
report.set_image("initial_texture", initial_texture, description="Initial texture.")

Read structured entries through report.values[name].value, report.tables[name].rows and report.images[name].pixels. report.directory is the workspace for additional files. It is None for in-memory output. The OfflineReport API defines supported values and name validation.

The framework persists partial reports on failure and restores completed reports during resume. Experiments defines checkpoint behavior. The CLI reference describes output locations and the evaluate rebuild.

docs.title: Supplied optimization paths
docs.text: PatchOptimization connects PatchAttack to driving scorers and candidate rendering. DetectorPatchOptimization and RolloutPatchOptimization configure the stop-sign white-box and black-box attacks. Their supplied settings and uses are in Physical patch and Stop-sign patch.

docs.title: Simulators
docs.text:
Audience: Experiment authors and simulator implementers.

Outcome: Choose simulator behavior and implement a custom simulator.

Prerequisites: Architecture.

docs.title: Simulator and simulator runtime
docs.text:
A Simulator stores configuration and capability declarations. Each create_runtime(seed) creates a SimulatorRuntime whose creator closes its world and connections, including after failures. Import interfaces from avsectester.closed_loop.simulators and concrete implementations from simulators.carla, simulators.nurec or simulators.recorded.

reset initializes a selected ScenarioStart and captures its first observation. step advances one decision and captures again. observe copies the current capture without rendering, advancing time or invoking hooks. state copies physical ego, actors and inserted objects.

Only world settings reach reset. Sensor corruptions apply after capture. See Environments for environment composition and Python API for signatures and errors.

docs.title: Scenario start inputs
docs.text: The dataset supplies ScenarioStart. Attack selection metadata is not a simulator input.

docs.title: Read prescribed motion
docs.text:
start_replay initializes and captures a recorded or recipe boundary with prescribed ego motion. advance_replay advances that motion and captures without stage hooks. Replay rejects bound hooks. Advancement also requires an initialized runtime and replay capability.

Simulator Prescribed-motion advancement Past observations CARLA Supported Unsupported Recorded playback Supported Unsupported NuRec Unsupported Supported

Services reuse forward scans where advancement is supported. NuRec instead resets prescribed motion at each requested frame.

docs.title: Inserted world objects
docs.text:
insert_object registers an ObjectAsset under a unique ID and rigid world pose. remove_object removes it. The physical state().objects changes immediately, while images change at the next capture. Inserted objects stay separate from native actors, have zero velocity and do not participate in native physics or collisions.

Shared camera composition projects the asset, resolves nearest surfaces and applies visibility. The returned camera view contains composed RGB. Existing depth becomes the pixelwise minimum of native and object depth. A view without native depth keeps depth=None.

Simulator Occlusion CARLA Aligned scene depth for depth_camera, actor cuboids for other cameras NuRec Reconstruction visibility from rendered probes, or mesh/actor geometry Recorded playback Actor cuboids. Not yet implemented. Static-scene occlusion. See Recorded static occlusion.

SensorView.composition records the unmodified background and its CompositePlan. plan.apply(background) reproduces the capture. Differentiable composition follows the same calculation where all harmonizers support it. See Optimization and the compositing API.

Occlusion tolerance keeps scene surfaces within the configured tolerance in front of an object from hiding it. The same rule applies to geometry and reconstruction probes. Option defaults are listed in the configuration reference.

object_visibility describes the latest capture. A projected but fully hidden object has a camera entry with zero visible pixels. An object outside a camera projection has no entry. SensorView.objects holds the corresponding immutable placed objects. Captures retain their own object membership until the next capture.

See Writing attacks for insertion actions and Runtime records for saved evidence.

Not yet implemented. Inserted objects in non-camera sensors. See TODO.

docs.title: CARLA
docs.text:
A CarlaDataset supplies recipes describing map, spawns, sensors and prescribed motion. CarlaSimulator supplies the connection and synchronous timing settings. Each reset requires a recipe-bearing ScenarioStart and uses a dedicated server.

Traffic-light states are recorded under OpenDRIVE control IDs.

docs.title: Selected-origin initialization
docs.text:
The runtime creates actors and sensors, replays prescribed motion to the deployment window, applies setup actions and runs the deployment tick budget before capturing the selected boundary. At position zero, actors are held during setup ticks. Before decision zero, ego is released from recipe motion for driving-system control. See the deployment tick budget.

A positive selected boundary needs materialized frame data. Recorded initialization evidence preserves the selected actor identities and sensor timing. See Experiments for preparation and Runtime for decision order.

Setting depth_camera selects an RGB camera for aligned depth and an undistorted pinhole lens. Other sensors keep their configured capture types. CARLA LiDAR retains native byte axes and its wrapper's flipy setting. See LiDAR records.

docs.title: NuRec
docs.text:
NuRec requires a ScenarioStart from its dataset. The runtime initializes the recorded pose, timeline and actors, then advances ego with the selected dynamics. Camera names remain native unless camera_aliases maps them to observation names. Aliases also apply to views and calibration.

Not yet implemented. NuRec and recorded-playback traffic-light state recording. See Traffic-light states.

Constructing mesh-depth or ground-contact support requires the nurec extra. Reset checks required archive meshes before connecting to NRE. Missing resources fail preflight. A manually started NRE must enable --enable-editing-actors.

The decision step comes from dataset.time_step through configuration loading. A driving system can require a specific step. See Configuration for the injection and consistency rules.

NRE is required for camera rendering. See automatic local services for CLI and Python use.

Construction does not connect to NRE:

from avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.ego_dynamics import AlpaSimController
from avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.nurec import NuRecRenderer, NuRecSimulator

simulator = NuRecSimulator(
    NuRecRenderer(endpoint="127.0.0.1:50051"),
    AlpaSimController(),
    time_step=0.1,
    depth="none",
    physics_update_mode="none",
)
assert simulator.command_modes == frozenset({"trajectory"})

docs.title: Recorded past observations
docs.text:
After reset, observe_past(count) returns actual recorded observations before the selected start, oldest first, with negative run-relative timestamps and frames. It rejects insufficient history and preserves the current world, clock and capture. Start eligibility uses the larger history requirement of the simulator and DrivingAdapter.

Past captures use recorded ego poses and actors, including the same short-track filtering as current captures. Objects installed during reset or setup are composed using those recorded camera poses. Later insertions and actor overrides are excluded. Past captures bypass stage hooks and sensor attack actions. The runner applies sensor corruptions at each absolute dataset position, then passes history directly to AVStack.reset. It bypasses localization and the observation pipeline. See initialization records and environment randomness.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Map navigation matches the recorded ego path to driving lanes and extends the route through successors. Every capture projects the current physical ego origin onto that route and provides forward points in ego coordinates. Navigation expresses intent. It does not constrain the produced or executed command.

Recorded-route mode uses the recording without extension. Disabled navigation supplies no route. A map route needs driving lanes. Folded or inconsistent routes are rejected by validate_start so selection can record the reason. With loaded metadata, an invalid segment fails preparation. Algorithm parameters and constraints are in the navigation API.

docs.title: Ground contact
docs.text:
The runtime retains a three-dimensional ego pose. Ground contact fits the predicted box bottom to the selected scene mesh after each dynamics step. Rejected corrections retain the prediction. Termination events count failures by reason. Disabling physical updates retains the dynamics prediction.

The full scene mesh may include roadside objects. A ground-only mesh avoids using those surfaces for ego contact where that asset is available. Ground contact is an approximate fit rather than a penetration solver. It does not correct traffic actors.

docs.title: Camera resolution
docs.text:
The renderer probes each configured camera when loading a scene and scales its lens to the image dimensions actually returned by NRE. NRE preserves aspect ratio, so returned width can differ from the request. Subsequent captures must retain those dimensions.

Captures render a single instant.

Not yet implemented. Rolling-shutter exposure. See TODO.

The lens includes its f-theta model and recorded windshield distortion. Camera projection, mesh depth and object placement share the resulting geometry. Camera coordinate conventions and models are specified in the Python API.

docs.title: Move recorded actors
docs.text:
Only controllable tracks can be moved by NRE. Parked tracks stay at recorded poses and set_actor_state rejects them. Short controllable tracks are filtered by min_track_duration_s. Zero disables filtering.

Filtered controllable tracks are absent from world snapshots, sensor actors, depth and metrics. All captures and probes hide their recorded render instances below the scene. Parked tracks are never duration-filtered.

An accepted override changes world state immediately and camera state at the next capture. Its explicit world velocity advances the actor at fixed orientation until reset or another override. control_actor is unsupported. Without traffic simulation, checkpoints preserve actor overrides. Restoring a checkpoint creates a new capture of the restored state.

docs.title: Reactive traffic
docs.text:
Enable AlpaSimTraffic through simulator.options.traffic. YAML, timing and history follow Reactive traffic configuration.

World actors begin with unfiltered recorded states, then use returned controllable-session poses, then explicit overrides. Parked tracks stay at recorded poses within recorded support. Sessions include duration-qualified tracks with nonempty clipped history. A first override backfills constant-velocity history and subsequent requests resend its complete history.

Trajectories are not smoothed. Offline candidate rollouts also require the service.

Not yet implemented. Fitting traffic actors to the selected ground mesh, checkpointing traffic sessions and controlling CATK sampling through the caller seed. See Traffic actor ground contact.

docs.title: Ego dynamics
docs.text:
Dynamics Commands Behavior KinematicBicycle Actuator Integrates a kinematic bicycle TrajectoryFollower Trajectory Follows planned positions ideally AlpaSimController Trajectory Tracks a trajectory with AlpaSim's controller and vehicle model

NuRec initializes longitudinal/lateral speed, yaw rate and acceleration from the recorded trajectory before resetting dynamics. The three-dimensional ego geometry still comes from the dataset.

AlpaSimController uses AlpaSim Ford Fusion vehicle parameters.

Trajectory commands use rig-frame poses and increasing timestamps, beginning at the current origin. The controller tracks the full forecast. It need not execute its first planned acceleration exactly. There is no automatic command conversion.

A custom dynamics component supplies step and may supply reset and command_modes. Each runtime receives its own copy. Constructor defaults and trajectory constraints are listed in the dynamics API.

docs.title: Mesh depth
docs.text:
Mesh depth combines archived static surfaces and current actor cuboids. Calibrated camera rays keep the nearest hit, expressed as optical-axis depth. Missing hits are infinite. Actor extents must be known. Depth is computed lazily per camera and cached for the capture.

Mesh content is not classified or erased when an actor moves. Archived vehicle geometry can therefore continue to occlude its recorded location. Cuboid silhouettes can differ from rendered vehicles. Rendered probes instead measure the reconstruction's visibility directly.

docs.title: Rendered-probe occlusion
docs.text:
Opaque white and black probe copies measure whether scene content hides inserted surfaces. Only sufficiently opaque asset pixels contribute probes. The renderer requires a client probe directory visible inside the NRE service. Path and mount rules are in Configuration.

Not yet implemented. Published asset conventions for all probe axes, scaling and padding. See NuRec rendered-probe conventions.

A captured composition.plan already contains this measured visibility. An arbitrary replacement object list needs a fresh render request. SensorView.composite_plan cannot obtain new reconstruction probes from a detached view. Geometry mode can build plans from its supplied depth and actors.

docs.title: Recorded playback
docs.text: RecordedReplaySimulator captures supported dataset frames while ego and other actors follow their recorded motion. Commands do not change that trajectory. It supports camera aliases and shared world-object composition. Environment support follows Configuration.

docs.title: Write a custom simulator
docs.text:
See the simulator base module for its Extension contract. Architecture describes the world-claim and operation-isolation rules.

Subclass Simulator for configuration and SimulatorRuntime for native world operations. Declare dataset kinds, timing, command modes, stages, world settings, capture capabilities and identity.

Declare every view-capable sensor in sensors and cameras in camera_sensors. Native views supply capture data and sensor geometry. The shared runtime owns camera composition. A lightweight sensor_geometry implementation avoids image/depth work for projection-only requests. Past-capable implementations supply recorded observations and recorded camera views for start-object composition.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Configure timing and rendering in Configuration.
  • Bind a driving system.
  • Use world insertion actions.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Audience: Experiment operators.

Outcome: Look up commands, options, output files and exit codes.

Prerequisites: Installation.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Use the configured Compose experiment service. NuRec commands are:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment version
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml --prepared DIRECTORY
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml --resume
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment evaluate CONFIG.yaml
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment nre serve CONFIG.yaml --gpu N
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment nre stop CONFIG.yaml
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment trafficsim serve CONFIG.yaml --gpu N --models models/alpasim-trafficsim
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment trafficsim stop CONFIG.yaml

For an already started CARLA experiment service, use docker compose exec carla-experiment avsectester COMMAND. The quickstart provides first-run examples.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
run CONFIG.yaml loads configuration, prepares artifacts, executes treatments and evaluates saved evidence. It requires a nonempty attack mapping and runs.output. The configuration reference describes YAML keys, defaults and preparation compatibility.

Option Default Meaning --prepared DIRECTORY omitted Load a complete preparation into a fresh output directory --resume false Continue preparation and execution in runs.output --nre-gpu N AVSECTESTER_HOST_GPU GPU for an automatically started NRE --nre-name NAME avsectester-nre-PORT Name of an automatically started NRE container --trafficsim-gpu N AVSECTESTER_HOST_GPU GPU for automatically started traffic --trafficsim-models DIR omitted Local model directory required when starting traffic --trafficsim-name NAME avsectester-trafficsim-PORT Name of an automatically started traffic container --service-timeout SECONDS 600 Positive service startup timeout

A nonempty output directory is rejected without --resume. --prepared and --resume are mutually exclusive.

docs.title: Preparation reuse
docs.text: --prepared maps to loading a complete preparation. --resume continues saved preparation and execution. See Experiments for validation, resume and persistence semantics.

docs.title: Automatic local services
docs.text:
With reactive traffic enabled, provide its local weights when a service may need starting:

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment run CONFIG.yaml --trafficsim-models models/alpasim-trafficsim

run checks the configured NuRec renderer and traffic endpoints after configuration, output and preparation checks. A running service must contain every configured dataset scene. A compatible service is reused and left running. A scene mismatch is an error.

Missing services can start only on local endpoints: 127.0.0.1, localhost, 0.0.0.0 or ::1. Starting traffic requires --trafficsim-models. GPU selection uses the explicit service option or AVSECTESTER_HOST_GPU, which the NuRec Compose service sets from NUREC_GPU. The value must be one nonnegative host GPU index. This selects the physical device independently of the model's YAML device option.

Python callers start required services themselves, for example with local_services.

Managed services cover preparation, execution and evaluation. Startup, reuse and shutdown each print a progress line. On completion, exceptions or Ctrl-C, only containers started by this command are stopped and removed, in reverse startup order. Cleanup errors are attached to an active exception. After a completed experiment they are reported without replacing its result. A killed command can leave its exited container behind. The next start removes it, following the NRE rules for existing containers.

NRE startup creates its client probe directory. Docker mounts each archive read-only at /mnt/nre-data/<filename> and mounts the probe directory at server_probe_directory, or at the same absolute client path when that option is null. Archive filenames must be unique. The Compose host-path and Docker access setup is described in Installation.

The optional manual service commands below support reuse across multiple experiments.

docs.title: Evaluate
docs.text:
evaluate CONFIG.yaml reads runs.output, recomputes metrics and replaces evaluation outputs. It leaves run logs and preparation unchanged. It uses saved segments, maps and the metadata hash. The dataset, external metadata file, model inference and simulator services are not needed.

Metric configuration may change before reevaluation, subject to the saved compatibility rules. Corrupt individual run logs are recorded as failures while other runs remain available. Saved directories for removed or unexpected treatments are reported and skipped.

Both run and evaluate print offline_report.html and evaluation_report.html paths. Evaluate rebuilds both pages from saved files. See Evaluation for terminal summaries, statistics and unavailable values.

docs.title: NRE
docs.text:
nre serve CONFIG --gpu N [--name NAME] [--image IMAGE] [--cache-size 2] [--timeout 600] [--dry-run] loads the configuration, starts Docker and waits for Serving on.

Option Default --gpu N required host GPU index --name NAME avsectester-nre-PORT --image IMAGE nvcr.io/nvidia/nre/nre-ga:26.04 --cache-size K 2 --timeout SECONDS 600 --dry-run false

The configuration must contain NuRecDataset and NuRecRenderer with a local endpoint. This command does not validate experiment environments. Archive and probe mounts follow the automatic service rules.

docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment nre serve configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_alpamayo_2601.yaml --gpu N
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment nre serve configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_alpamayo_2601.yaml --gpu N --dry-run
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment nre stop configs/nurec_stop_sign_patch_alpamayo_2601.yaml

--dry-run prints a shell-quoted Docker command without creating directories or containers and does not require Docker on PATH. A normal launch requires Docker. An exited container with the chosen name that an earlier AVSecTester start by the same user created is removed first. Any other container with that name is left untouched and reported as an error. Successful startup prints endpoint, GPU, scene count, container name and the corresponding stop command.

Startup failure or timeout includes the last 50 log lines and removes the newly created container. The container is created without Docker's --rm so startup diagnostics remain readable.

nre stop CONFIG [--name NAME] derives the default name from the endpoint without enumerating dataset archives, then stops and removes that container. A missing container is an error.

docs.title: Trafficsim
docs.text:
trafficsim serve CONFIG --gpu N --models DIR [--name NAME] [--image IMAGE] [--timeout 600] [--dry-run] requires NuRecDataset and a configured AlpaSimTraffic with a local endpoint.

Option Default --gpu N required host GPU index --models DIR required model directory --name NAME avsectester-trafficsim-PORT --image IMAGE avsectester:trafficsim --timeout SECONDS 600 --dry-run false 
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment trafficsim serve CONFIG.yaml --gpu N --models models/alpasim-trafficsim
docker compose run --rm nurec-experiment trafficsim stop CONFIG.yaml

Archives are mounted read-only under /mnt/nre-data and models at /mnt/trafficsim-models. The server uses prediction_steps=15, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and MKL_NUM_THREADS=1. Readiness requires the CATK startup log followed by a successful metadata RPC. Startup errors, dry-run and existing container handling follow the NRE rules.

trafficsim stop CONFIG [--name NAME] derives the name without enumerating datasets, then stops and removes that container. Use the same explicit name for serve and stop. Reactive traffic behavior is described in Simulators.

docs.title: Interruptions
docs.text: Ctrl-C exits 130, cleans up owned containers and prints the output directory when available. Partial reports may remain. evaluate regenerates them without simulation. Checkpoint and retry behavior follow Resume interrupted work.

docs.title: Output layout
docs.text:
<output>/
  preparation-progress.json
  prepared.json
  attacks/<attack>/metadata.json
  attacks/<attack>/artifacts.pkl
  attacks/<attack>/manifest.json
  offline/<attack>/report.json
  offline/<attack>/<table>.csv
  offline/<attack>/<image-or-series>.png
  offline/<attack>/files/
  offline-incomplete/<attack>-<UTC timestamp>/
  offline_report.html
  maps/<scenario>.json
  runs/segment-<NNNNN>/seed-<S>/<treatment>/
  evaluation/report.json
  evaluation/runs.csv
  evaluation/plots/
  evaluation_report.html

Artifact filenames above describe the default trusted-pickle format. Attacks may override artifact persistence. Segment numbers are global unit indexes. Each run directory contains manifest.json, published Parquet step/event parts and payload shards belonging to its RunLog. Offline report content is described in Optimization, and evaluation content in Evaluation.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Command completed without failed runs, selection errors or metric errors. This does not establish attack effectiveness 1 Configuration load error, preparation load/validation error, selection, execution, result reading, metric evaluation or service startup/stop failed 2 Invalid configuration or metadata contents, output conflict or incompatible saved preparation 130 Keyboard interruption. Available partial output is retained

Service scene mismatch, a missing service at a nonlocal endpoint, absent --trafficsim-models and invalid GPU selection are configuration errors (exit 2). Container launch, readiness and explicit stop failures exit 1. Unsupported hook stages or incompatible commands fail the affected run at its start (exit 1). evaluate requires prepared.json and exits 1 if it is missing. With --prepared or --resume, the current hook simulator.setup ticks plus Attack.deployment_ticks(segment) must fit the saved deployment tick budget. Exceeding it fails execution with exit 1. See saved-preparation compatibility.

docs.title: Supplied configurations
docs.text: See the complete configuration list and configuration reference.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
Audience: Experiment authors.

Outcome: Construct a complete experiment from YAML or Python.

Prerequisites: Architecture.

docs.title: Experiment configuration
docs.text:
A configuration contains component specifications and run settings. YAML section order does not affect loading. load_configuration accepts a YAML path, a mapping or an ExperimentConfiguration object.

Every constructor specification uses type and optional options. A built-in short name selects a framework component. package.module:Class or package.module:function selects user code. dataset, simulator, avstack, attacks.<name>, evaluation.metrics entries and observation_pipeline can also reference YAML files. Nested constructors use the same type/options form. Type paths and hook imports execute Python code. Use only trusted sources.

docs.title: Component short names
docs.text:
Category and location Accepted names dataset.type CarlaDataset, NuRecDataset, NuScenesDataset simulator.type CarlaSimulator, NuRecSimulator, RecordedReplaySimulator avstack.type ModularAVStack, CameraForwardCollisionAVStack, AlpamayoAVStack, RuleBasedAVStack evaluation.metrics[].type DrivingMetrics, DetectionMetrics, TrajectoryDeviation, StopImpact, StopLineMetrics, ReasoningPhraseRate attacks.<name>.type Discovered Attack subclasses in class-name-derived directories environment.sensors[].type GaussianNoise, ShotNoise, Fog, Rain, Snow, Brightness, LowLight, Contrast, Gamma, ColorTemp, MotionBlur, DefocusBlur, JPEGCompression, ChromaticAberration, AlbumentationsCorruption

Nested type mappings construct only dataset, simulator, driving-system and metric short names from this table, or module:name paths. Attack names, corruption names and other values pass through as native data.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning device omitted Default for constructors with an explicit device parameter dataset required Scenario source metadata save/load both null Export or load one shared segment file split null Training, validation and test segment allocation simulator required World and sensor provider avstack required Driving system and optional bindings attacks required, nonempty Names mapped to Attack specifications hooks null Stage handlers shared by all treatments evaluation automatic metric set Metric specifications runs defaults below Treatments, seeds, environment, recording and output

This complete example uses the checkout's memory components and needs no simulator service or model weights. Supplied simulator configurations use the same structure. See the configuration list.

device: cpu
dataset:
  type: tests.fakes:MemoryDataset
  options: {decision_steps: 6, time_step: 0.1}
simulator:
  type: tests.fakes:MemorySimulator
avstack:
  type: tests.fakes:ConstantAVStack
  options:
    command:
      type: avsectester.data_types:Control
      options: {throttle: 0.2}
attacks:
  probe:
    type: tests.fakes:MinimalAttack
    options: {decision_steps: 2, max_segments: 1}
evaluation:
  metrics:
    - {type: DrivingMetrics}
runs:
  treatments:
    - {name: clean}
    - {name: probe, attack_name: probe}
  seeds: [0]
  recording:
    sensor_ids: [front]
    representations: [model_input]
    every_n_steps: 1
  output: results/memory

docs.title: Device
docs.text:
The optional top-level device is a nonempty string, such as cuda:0. It supplies a default to every type/options constructor whose signature explicitly declares device. An explicit option wins. Constructors without that parameter, including those accepting only **kwargs, receive nothing extra. Omitting the key preserves each constructor's default.

Injection applies to dataset, simulator, AVStack, observation pipeline, bindings, attacks, hooks, metrics and sensor corruptions, including nested constructors and deferred AVStack construction. Directly supplied Python objects are unchanged. The injected options have the same preparation identity as explicitly written options.

Components with this parameter include AlpamayoAVStack, YOLOXDetector, DetectorPatchOptimization, PatchOptimization and PCTNetHarmonizer. Container GPU selection is separate. See automatic local services.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text: dataset selects the scenario source. NuRecDataset accepts either dataroot, searched recursively for USDZ archives, or an explicit usdz_paths sequence. The two options are mutually exclusive. Dataset behavior and semantic maps are described in Datasets.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
The JSON file contains format: "avsectester.metadata", version: 1, dataset_type: "module:Class" and segments encoded by DEFAULT_REGISTRY. The dataset type must match. See Experiments for save, load and validation timing.

metadata.save and metadata.load both default to null and are mutually exclusive. Paths resolve relative to the containing YAML file. Python configurations use MetadataConfiguration.

metadata:
  save: ../results/metadata/stop_sign_2601.json

metadata:
  load: ../results/metadata/stop_sign_2601.json

Duplicate complete segments are rejected on save and load. There are no per-attack or per-treatment overrides. The preparation records the source path and raw-byte SHA256. Compatibility depends only on that hash, so moving an unchanged file is allowed. Changing any bytes, including whitespace, changes its identity. Reusing preparation for execution checks the current file's hash and rechecks saved segment frames. Other checks follow Input validation. Reevaluation uses the saved hash and segments without reading this file. Adding or removing metadata.load relative to the saved configuration is incompatible.

The Python API provides save_metadata and load_metadata for user-generated segments. The experiment workflow describes preparation reuse.

docs.title: Data split
docs.text:
Without split, each attack receives all its selected segments in its offline phase and all units are executed. With split:

split:
  train_segments: 5
  validation_segments: 0
  seed: 0
  execute: [test]
Key Default Meaning train_segments required Positive number of training units validation_segments 0 Nonnegative number of validation units seed 0 Nonnegative permutation seed execute [test] Unique subset of train, validation and test. An empty list executes no units

Unknown keys are rejected. Executing validation requires a positive validation count. Training plus validation must be smaller than the number of units, leaving at least one test unit.

A unit matches on scenario, start, stop and all user_data, encoded as canonical JSON. Units follow dataset scenario order, then start, stop and configured attack order. A seeded NumPy permutation assigns training units first, validation units next and test units last. Identical selections share a part. The same window with different user_data forms separate units. Training and test may therefore contain the same captured scene.

OfflineContext.metadata contains training segments and validation_metadata contains validation segments, each in selection order. PreparedExperiment.metadata keeps all selections and units records the part and selecting attacks. split.execute affects execution, not preparation compatibility.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
CARLA scene and prescribed motion settings belong to CarlaRecipe. CarlaSimulator receives the runtime client settings. For recorded sources, choose a simulator compatible with the dataset. Simulators describes their behavior.

A simulator's top-level time_step parameter inherits dataset.time_step when omitted and when the dataset provides it. This injection does not recurse into nested constructors. Explicit values are retained, but ExperimentConfiguration rejects a dataset/simulator mismatch.

docs.title: NuRec closed-loop settings
docs.text:
NuRecSimulator requires a renderer and a non-null time_step. The loader supplies the latter from NuRecDataset. Reset requires ScenarioStart. Constructor defaults are:

Option Default Accepted values or role dynamics KinematicBicycle() Ego-dynamics implementation camera_aliases empty Native camera ID to observation/sensor-view name. Output names must be unique depth mesh mesh, none route_generator map map, recorded, none physics_update_mode ego_only ego_only, none ground_mesh mesh mesh, mesh_ground object_occlusion rendered_probes rendered_probes, geometry occlusion_tolerance_m 0.15 Nonnegative scene occlusion tolerance in meters traffic null Optional AlpaSimTraffic min_track_duration_s 3.0 Nonnegative moving-track duration threshold. A value of 0 disables filtering

nurec_patch.yaml, nurec_speed_feedback.yaml and nurec_object_insertion.yaml use ground_mesh: mesh and the default mesh depth. The four stop-sign configurations use ground_mesh: mesh_ground and depth: none. All seven explicitly select map navigation and ego ground contact with AlpaSimController.

simulator:
  type: NuRecSimulator
  options:
    depth: none
    route_generator: map
    physics_update_mode: ego_only
    ground_mesh: mesh_ground
    renderer:
      type: avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.nurec:NuRecRenderer
      options:
        endpoint: 127.0.0.1:50051
        cameras: [camera_front_wide_120fov]
        probe_directory: ../results/nre-probes
        server_probe_directory: /mnt/nre-probes
    dynamics:
      type: avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.ego_dynamics:AlpaSimController

NuRec cameras render at their native resolution. probe_directory is a client-side path resolved relative to the YAML file. server_probe_directory is an unchanged string in the server's filesystem namespace. The server must be able to read the probe files. See automatic local services for startup and mounts.

docs.title: Reactive traffic
docs.text:
Add the following under simulator.options:

traffic:
  type: avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.nurec:AlpaSimTraffic
  options:
    endpoint: 127.0.0.1:6200
    history_steps: 16
    rpc_timeout_s: 300.0

Traffic defaults to null. Enabling it requires 0.1 s decisions and history_steps - 1 preceding recorded decisions. Traffic configuration affects preparation identity. metadata.load can share segments between modes. Services are managed by run.

docs.title: Driving specification
docs.text:
avstack.type selects an AVStack class or factory. Its options are passed to each fresh instance. A constructor declaring seed receives the run seed. Explicitly writing that reserved option is an error. The top-level device follows the device rule.

Key under avstack Meaning type Required AVStack class or callable options Constructor arguments, empty by default observation_pipeline Optional ObservationPipeline type/options specification command_modes Optional assertion matching the stack's declared modes bindings Optional binding factory, with type/options

AVStack.decision_time_step optionally declares a fixed cadence. DrivingAdapter reads it from factory.avstack_type, or uses its explicit fallback without constructing the stack. ClosedLoopServices rejects a driving-system step that differs from the simulator step. AlpamayoAVStack requires 0.1 s decisions. Its supplied configurations use frame_subsample: 1 to select camera frames from history without changing decision timing. See Past observations.

A binding has signature function(avstack_factory, **options) -> DrivingAdapter. The factory exposes avstack_type and an independent read-only avstack_options mapping. Bindings declare components and scorers without constructing the stack. Driving systems describes the supplied bindings.

docs.title: Attack specification
docs.text:
attacks is a nonempty mapping of names to Attack specifications or YAML paths. Each entry has type, optional options and optional environment. Each attack selects its own segments unless metadata.load supplies them. See Writing attacks for lifecycle phases and implementer responsibilities. Attacks that do not override build_metadata require metadata.load.

attacks:
  speed_feedback:
    type: SpeedFeedbackAttack
    options: {decision_steps: 20, target_speed: 3.0, gain: 0.1, max_bias: 5.0}
    environment:
      world: {weather: SoftRainNoon}

See the configuration list for supplied attacks and component construction for user type paths.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
hooks is a sequence of stage handlers shared by every treatment. Each mapping declares stage and exactly one of type or native_hook. A type-based hook accepts options. Optional imports lists modules imported before constructing the handler.

hooks:
  - stage: perception.post
    imports: [my_project.hooks]
    native_hook:
      type: MyDetectionHook

Native hooks require a .pre or .post stage. Their payload uses avstack's HOOKS registry format and does not accept a separate options key. Modules listed in imports must register the hook in HOOKS. Stage semantics belong to Runtime.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
evaluation.metrics accepts Metric type/options specifications. Omitting it selects DrivingMetrics and TrajectoryDeviation, adding DetectionMetrics when every completed log provides canonical detections. An explicit empty list selects no metrics. Repeated metric types are rejected. DetectionMetrics is rejected during loading when the configured stack declares no detections.

Custom metrics use package.module:Class. See Experiment configuration.

evaluation:
  metrics:
    - {type: StopLineMetrics}
    - {type: ReasoningPhraseRate, options: {phrase: stop sign}}
    - {type: DrivingMetrics}

Metric fields and comparison semantics are described in Evaluation.

docs.title: Run settings
docs.text:
Run controls belong under runs, represented in Python by frozen RunsConfiguration.

Key Default Meaning treatments clean plus one treatment per attack Named runs with optional attack_name and environment seeds [0] Nonempty unique nonnegative integers decision_steps null Optional positive upper bound per selected segment environment empty Shared world and sensor settings recording defaults below Sensor payload retention output null Output directory, required by the CLI strict false Stop on the first execution or selection error

Attack and treatment names must be nonempty, contain no path separators and differ from . and ... Treatment names must be unique. A treatment without attack_name has no enabled attack. Otherwise that field must reference a configured attack. Group membership is defined in Evaluation.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
CARLA world settings accept weather as a preset name or parameter mapping, lighting, map_layers and road_friction. NuRec and recorded playback reject every nonempty world setting.

Environment YAML has world and sensors keys. The base is runs.environment, with optional attack and treatment overrides. Environments describes merge and validation behavior. Sensor entries use type, options and an optional camera. Omitting camera applies the corruption only to the first sensor_data entry, which must be a readable RGB image.

runs:
  environment:
    world: {weather: SoftRainNoon}
    sensors:
      - {type: GaussianNoise, options: {severity: 0.2}, camera: front}

Custom corruptions use package.module:Class. See Experiment configuration. Severity is in [0, 1] and defaults to 0.5. ColorTemp also accepts warm, which defaults to true. AlbumentationsCorruption requires transform. The Python API lists the available corruption classes.

docs.title: Recording
docs.text:
Key under recording Default Meaning sensor_ids [] Unique sensor names whose payloads are retained representations [model_input] Subset of raw and model_input every_n_steps 1 Positive decision interval for retained sensor payloads

Empty sensor_ids retains no image payloads. State, commands, actions, outputs, available components and detections are recorded every decision. Reevaluation cannot recover omitted sensor payloads.

runs:
  recording:
    sensor_ids: [front]
    representations: [raw, model_input]
    every_n_steps: 2

docs.title: Constructor filesystem parameters
docs.text:
Filesystem options follow constructor annotations for dataset, simulator, AVStack, attack, hook, metric and nested constructors. Path or os.PathLike annotations mark paths, including unions and sequence elements such as str | Path or list[Path].

Relative values become absolute strings resolved beside the YAML file that contains them. A leading ~ is expanded. Absolute paths preserve their location. URI strings containing :// are unchanged. Plain str, unannotated parameters, Any, **kwargs and untyped mappings do not trigger path resolution. Unresolvable annotations mentioning Path are errors. Make their names available at runtime. Other unresolved annotations are ignored.

Component YAML references and runs.output also resolve relative to their containing YAML file.

docs.title: Saved preparation compatibility
docs.text:
The saved identity includes dataset type/scenario IDs, simulator identity and each attack's type, parameters and environment. Its preparation record includes the first run seed, split counts/seed and merged offline environments.

Loading a preparation checks these values and recomputes saved units under the configured split. A current metadata file must have the saved raw-byte hash, but its path may differ. A mismatch raises ConfigurationMismatchError. Saved preparations require an offline report for every completed attack, including attacks whose offline phase is a no-op.

Additional seeds, treatments, recording, output, strict, decision limits, split.execute and evaluation settings may change. The first seed, partition and offline environments must match. run --prepared writes the loaded preparation record, units, deployment budget and metadata source unchanged into the new output. AVStack and hook configurations are not part of saved-preparation compatibility. Attack constructor options are compared as written, including an explicitly written default versus an omitted option. Lists and tuples with identical contents compare equally. Booleans, integers and floating-point numbers remain distinct, so true, 1 and 1.0 are incompatible. The current hooks' setup ticks plus the attack's deployment requirement must not exceed the saved deployment tick budget. Execution fails otherwise.

YAML declarations retain their constructor options. Direct Python attacks describe their inputs through configuration_parameters(). An undescribable value produces a warning and marks parameters unverified. Loading or evaluating that preparation is then rejected.

Reevaluation checks the saved identity and uses saved metadata and maps without accessing the external metadata file or the dataset. Workflow details are in Experiments. Commands and exit codes are in CLI.

docs.title: Constraints and errors
docs.text:
CameraCalibration does not validate its array at construction. Producers and consumers validate transforms. WindshieldDistortion raises ValueError when a polynomial length is not a triangular number (order + 1)(order + 2) / 2.

FThetaCamera.unproject raises NotImplementedError without pixeldist_to_angle and evaluates that inverse polynomial directly rather than solving the forward polynomial. A singular screen correction (c - d * e == 0) is not rejected and yields non-finite rays.

docs.title: Constraints and errors
docs.text:
read_clipgt raises ImportError without pyarrow and applies no coordinate transform. Lane rails remain recorded boundaries. Centerline construction resamples both at matching normalized arc-length fractions, using the larger point count, then takes paired midpoints. Connectivity and control/line associations require source records.

Lane classification applies in order: SHOULDER_LANE gives shoulder, PARKING_LANE gives parking, vehicle_types containing CAR gives driving, only BICYCLE gives bike and anything else gives other. HOV_LANE and SERVICE_ROAD with CAR remain driving.

Exact traffic-sign categories TRAFFIC_SIGN_REGULATORY_R1_STOP, TRAFFIC_SIGN_REGULATORY_R1_YIELD and TRAFFIC_SIGN_REGULATORY_R2_SPEED_LIMIT map to stop_sign, yield_sign and speed_limit. Other categories become other and retain their source native_category. An empty or unsupported traffic-light table does not make the whole mixed traffic_controls layer unavailable.

Only wait-line rows explicitly marked is_implicit=False are retained. All-implicit rows mean a known empty stop_lines layer. native_category keeps paint labels such as STOP. Subtypes ENTRY, NOT_APPLICABLE and CROSSWALK_ENTRY are neither categories nor filters. StopLine.kind comes only from explicit control/lane associations, never paint or nearest geometry. Multiple controls of one recognized kind may establish the kind. control_id requires one unique control. Missing or ambiguous evidence gives unknown. Missing or unusable geometry is reported in unavailable_layers.

docs.title: Constraints and errors
docs.text:
read_opendrive returns Unavailable without the CARLA client package and raises ValueError for empty text or an empty map name. Canonical conversion reflects the Y axis. Every lane type is sampled at spacing at most two meters on the center and both boundaries. Native midpoint refinement handles continuous geometry. Unresolved source discontinuities subdivide the existing straight connector while preserving its endpoints. Left/right neighbors refer only to the same travel direction.

Landmark types 206, 205, 274 and 1000001 map to stop_sign, yield_sign, speed_limit and traffic_light. Each stopping-control signal reference resolves its own road and governed lanes. A stop line spans each controlled lane perpendicular to its local heading, with ID stop-line:<signal_id>:<road_id>:<lane_id>. TrafficControl.lane_ids unions those references. stop_line_id is set only for one line. Otherwise follow StopLine.control_id. StopLine.native_category is opendrive_signal_reference.

Control orientation opposes the mean normalized governed-lane direction when its horizontal magnitude is at least 0.5. Otherwise it is the converted landmark heading plus 180° about local Z. Extent is (0, width, height). Unavailable thickness and unconfirmed speed limits are reported in unavailable_layers.
