docs.title: Constraints and errors
docs.text:
ExposureHarmonizer raises ValueError for a reference other than ring or under, a negative ring_px or feather_sigma, or a gain_range that is not two positive finite values in increasing order. Its tensor methods raise ValueError for images that are not CHW RGB, a mask that is not HW, mismatched devices or dtypes, or a nominal composite that differs from the composite in shape, dtype or device. They raise TypeError for non-floating images or a non-boolean mask.

ExposureHarmonizer converts sRGB c to linear l: l = c/12.92 for c ≤ 0.04045, otherwise l = ((c + 0.055)/1.055)^2.4. Luminance is Y = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B. The gain is g = clip(mean(Y_reference) / (mean(Y_nominal_visible) + 1e-6), gain_range). The reference is the ring_px-wide ring around the mask (ring) or the original background under the object (under). The NumPy __call__ uses the composite itself as the nominal composite. Visible linear RGB is multiplied by g and encoded as sRGB: c = 12.92l for l ≤ 0.0031308, otherwise c = 1.055l^(1/2.4) − 0.055. An empty visible or reference region returns the input unchanged. With feather_sigma above zero, output = a × adjusted + (1 − a) × background inside the mask, where a is the mask blurred by a Gaussian with that sigma.

PCTNetHarmonizer falls back to CPU when CUDA is unavailable. Explicit weights take precedence. Otherwise it uses <libcom_directory>/libcom/image_harmonization/pretrained_models/PCTNet.pth, downloading PCTNet.pth from BCMIZB/Libcom_pretrained_models through huggingface_hub into that directory on first use when the file is absent. With strict=True, a loading or inference failure raises RuntimeError. Otherwise ClassicHarmonizer handles that frame.

docs.title: Extension contract
docs.text:
Implement Harmonizer.__call__(composite_rgb, mask, background_rgb) for aligned H×W×3 uint8 RGB arrays. The H×W mask marks visible pixels with nonzero values. The framework passes uint8 0/255. Return matching RGB shape and dtype, preserve mask-exterior pixels and leave inputs unchanged.

For differentiable composition, declare differentiable=True and implement harmonize_tensor(composite, mask, background, nominal_composite). The image tensors are CHW floating RGB in [0, 1] with matching shape, dtype and device. The HW mask is boolean. Return values in [0, 1]. CompositePlan.composite clamps its result to that range. Preserve gradients to candidate colors and mask-exterior pixels. Every harmonizer in a plan receives the same unadjusted composite and original background. The nominal composite shows each surface's nominal_texture when set and the candidate colors elsewhere, so exposure estimation can use the unpatched face as reference. The base method raises NotImplementedError.

General COCO object detection and differentiable confidence scoring with YOLOX.

Name and signature Meaning YOLOXDetector(weights_path: str | Path, model_name: str = "yolox-m", input_size: int = 1280, score_threshold: float = .5, nms_iou: float = .45, device: str = "cuda:0", model: Any = None) Detect COCO objects and score labeled target boxes using a local YOLOX checkpoint. YOLOXDetector.target_scores(images: torch.Tensor, targets: Sequence[TargetSpec]) -> torch.Tensor Return one differentiable pre-NMS confidence per BCHW image and target. YOLOXDetector.close() -> None Release the model. A closed detector cannot detect or score again.

docs.title: Constraints and errors
docs.text:
YOLOXDetector raises ValueError for a nonpositive input_size, a score_threshold outside [0, 1], or nms_iou outside (0, 1]. Loading raises FileNotFoundError for missing weights. An injected model that is not a torch.nn.Module raises TypeError. detect requires nonempty uint8 RGB (H, W, 3). target_scores requires finite floating RGB (B, 3, H, W) in [0, 1] and B targets, each with a COCO class name and finite nonempty xyxy box. Invalid inputs or mismatched batch lengths raise ValueError. Model outputs other than (B, N, 85) raise ValueError. Calling either method after close raises RuntimeError.

Images are reduced to at most input_size on the longest side, without upscaling, then converted to BGR × 255 and padded on the right and bottom with 114 to multiples of 32. Deployment uses class-wise NMS. Differentiable scores use the target class before NMS, selecting the largest objectness × class probability among anchors with IoU at least 0.3. No match returns an input-connected zero.

docs.title: avsectester.closed_loop.sensor_corruptions
docs.text:
Image-space sensor corruptions used by experiment environments.

Name and signature Meaning CORRUPTIONS = {c.__name__: c for c in (Fog, Rain, Snow, Brightness, LowLight, Contrast, Gamma, ColorTemp, GaussianNoise, ShotNoise, MotionBlur, DefocusBlur, JPEGCompression, ChromaticAberration)} Mapping from configuration names to the supplied sensor corruption classes. Corruption(severity: float = 0.5) One image-space corruption. apply(rgb, rng) -> rgb maps an (H,W,3) uint8 RGB frame to a corrupted one. severity in [0, 1] scales the corruption strength (0 ≈ identity). Corruption.category: str = "sensor" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. Corruption.name: str Configuration name identifying this corruption. Corruption.apply(rgb: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray Abstract. Transform one sensor payload using the supplied random generator. Fog(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Atmospheric haze: blend toward a bright airlight and flatten contrast (uniform, depth-free). Fog.category = "weather" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. Rain(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Darken, then add motion-blurred bright streaks (procedural). Rain.category = "weather" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. Snow(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Bright speckles plus a slight brighten and blur (procedural). Snow.category = "weather" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. Brightness(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Multiplicative brightening (over-exposure / bright sun). Brightness.category = "lighting" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. LowLight(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Night / underexposure: darken and add read noise (a dark sensor is a noisy sensor). LowLight.category = "lighting" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. Contrast(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Reduce contrast toward the frame mean (flat, washed-out light). Contrast.category = "lighting" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. Gamma(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Non-linear tone shift (darker mid-tones), as from a different exposure curve. Gamma.category = "lighting" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. ColorTemp(severity: float = 0.5, warm: bool = True) Subclass of Corruption. Color-cast shift — warm (default, sodium street-lights / sunset) or cool. ColorTemp.category = "lighting" Environment corruption category used to group related sensor effects. GaussianNoise(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Additive Gaussian read noise. ShotNoise(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Poisson (photon shot) noise — signal-dependent, as in low light. MotionBlur(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Directional blur from ego/scene motion (random angle, length scales with severity). DefocusBlur(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Out-of-focus blur (Gaussian, radius scales with severity). JPEGCompression(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Lossy-compression block artefacts (encoder quality drops with severity). ChromaticAberration(severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Lateral color fringing — shift the red and blue channels apart. AlbumentationsCorruption(transform: str, severity: float = 0.5) Subclass of Corruption. Named Albumentations transform with deterministic, severity-scaled parameters.

docs.title: Extension contract
docs.text:
Implement Simulator.create_runtime(seed) and declare dataset_kinds, capabilities, supported_stages, decision_time_step, command_modes, supported_world_settings, capture_ticks, past_steps and occlusion_tolerance_m on the configuration class.

Runtime subclasses implement _initialize_world(start, initialization, environment), _advance_native(control), _observe() and _state(). Optional native lifecycle methods are _sensor_view, _replay_tick, _observe_recorded, _recorded_sensor_geometry, _recorded_sensor_view, _capture_frame_data, _hold_tick, _replay_position, _check_initialization, _before_selected_capture, _replayed_scenario, _frame_data_provenance and _composite_plan. The default _hold_tick raises ValueError, so a runtime without it cannot hold an origin for deployment ticks. Defining reset, step, sensor_view, start_replay, advance_replay or observe_past in a subclass raises TypeError.

The default SimulatorRuntime.world_key is ("simulator", id(self)). For optical camera views, sensor_from_world = BODY_FROM_OPTICAL @ cam_from_world. setup_tick raises RuntimeError outside simulator.setup or after the deployment tick budget is exhausted.

docs.text:

Name and signature Meaning AdversarialSample(x: Tensor, target: data_types.TargetSpec, context: dict = dict()) One clean input to attack. context carries threat-model specifics — e.g. a patch's calibrated sampling grid and visibility mask — and is empty for a whole-image perturbation. DataSource.__getitem__(index: int) -> AdversarialSample Abstract. Return one sample. An out-of-range index raises IndexError. Perturbation() A threat model: the adversarial variable δ, how it enters the input, and its feasible set. Perturbation.init() -> Tensor Abstract. Return an initial δ (zeros / random) of this threat model's shape. Perturbation.apply(sample: AdversarialSample, delta: Tensor) -> Tensor Abstract. Form the adversarial input from a clean sample and δ (differentiable in δ). Perturbation.project(delta: Tensor) -> Tensor Abstract. Project δ back onto the feasible set (in place or returned). Perturbation.export(delta: Tensor) -> np.ndarray | None Physical realization of δ, if any — a patch returns (Hp,Wp,4) uint8. Default None. Perturbation.smoothness(delta: Tensor) -> Tensor Differentiable total variation of δ, weighted by an optimizer's smoothness term. Scorer() Score a batch with one score per input. Descriptors or objectives define the direction. Scorer.differentiable: bool = True Whether input-image gradients are supported by this component. Scorer.target_scores(images: Tensor, targets: Sequence[data_types.TargetSpec]) -> Tensor Abstract. Return one score per input. Mismatched input and target lengths raise ValueError. OptimizationObjective() Transform scores elementwise into losses to minimize. OptimizationObjective.loss(score: Tensor) -> Tensor Abstract. Map (B,) scores to (B,) losses with elementwise operations. HideObject() Subclass of OptimizationObjective. Suppress the target's detection by minimizing loss = score toward zero. HideBelowThreshold(threshold: float, margin: float = .1) Subclass of OptimizationObjective. Suppress a detection until its score is margin below the decision threshold. SpoofObject() Subclass of OptimizationObjective. Fabricate / keep a detection where the target box is: loss = 1 - score. OptimizationResult(delta: Tensor, export: np.ndarray | None, history: list[float], final_score: float) Output of optimization: PGD history is mean sample loss per epoch, and NES history is loss per step. GradientOptimizer() Optimization algorithm over a data source, perturbation, scorer and objective. GradientOptimizer.run(data: DataSource, perturbation: Perturbation, scorer: Scorer, objective: OptimizationObjective, *, monitor: Callable[[int, Tensor], None] | None = None) -> OptimizationResult Abstract. Optimize δ with exact input gradients in PGD or sampled gradient estimates in NES.

docs.text: HideBelowThreshold raises ValueError for a threshold or margin outside [0, 1]. Its loss is zero, with zero gradient, for scores below threshold - margin. OptimizationResult.final_score is the final scorer output, averaged over all samples for PGD and evaluated on the fixed sample for NES.

docs.text:
PatchPerturbation raises ValueError for a size that is not two positive integers, an init other than "random" or "gray", or an alpha that is not uint8 at the texture size. Its variable is CHW RGB in [0, 1], and projection clamps to that interval. apply reads mask and either plane_sampling or sampling_grid from sample.context. It raises ValueError when the mask is not (1, H, W), plane-sampling bounds leave the image, or the grid is not (H, W, 2). export returns HWC uint8 RGBA with the supplied alpha unchanged.

LinfImage starts from zero, projects each element into [−epsilon, epsilon] and clamps sample.x + delta into [0, 1]. Its export returns None.

docs.title: Constraints and errors
docs.text:
Overlapping session operations, a closed session or services, and reused component instances raise RuntimeError. Closing a session with an active operation also raises it. Reading sensor views or rendering raises NotImplementedError when the simulator does not support rendering. CandidateRequest raises ValueError when its decision count differs from its segment interval. Rollout raises ValueError for a seed differing from the session, a terminal frame differing from dataset.decision_window or deployment actions exceeding the shared budget.

Each evaluate call constructs a fresh AVStack. score calls in one session share one scoring AVStack. evaluate and score raise ValueError for an undeclared component or scorer. score(require_grad=True) also raises ValueError when the scorer declares no differentiable inputs or returns a value that does not require gradients.

docs.title: Constraints and errors
docs.text:
Stop-line distances are horizontal, positive before crossing and negative afterward. A run is assumed to start before its selected line.

The first crossing is None or (sample_index, fraction). Non-finite or non-N×3 positions, fewer than two finite 3D line points or no nonzero horizontal line segment raise ValueError.

docs.title: Extension contract
docs.text:
Implement run-level Metric.evaluate(group) to return a field mapping for each treatment name in the ComparisonGroup. Read only saved evidence and return missing values with reasons. Do not run inference or modify recorded runs. An overriding describe returns MetricDescription whose fields map each measured field name to a MetricField. evaluate_groups records another return type or an invalid field as a metric error.

Implement PairMetric.evaluate(pair) to return one scalar field mapping for the completed TreatmentPair. Missing evidence must produce UnavailableMetricValue with a reason rather than fabricated measurements. Describe those fields through describe.

docs.text:
DetectorPatchOptimization raises TypeError for an optimizer other than PGD and ValueError for an empty scorer_id or device, a samples_per_scene other than "all" or an integer of at least four, a nonpositive count, deceleration or progress_interval, or a confidence_margin outside [0, 1]. The closest trained route distance to the stop line is d_min = v² / (2a), where a is braking_deceleration_mps2.

RolloutPatchOptimization raises TypeError for an optimizer other than NES and ValueError for a nonpositive stop_speed_mps or max_training_segments, or a min_stop_command_step that is not a nonnegative integer. The offline phase raises ValueError when no training segment passes unpatched-replica calibration. See the black-box workflow for the calibration rules and query budget. docs.title: Runtime reference
docs.text:
Audience: Adapter and attack implementers.

Outcome: Look up decision order, stages, contexts and recorded evidence.

Prerequisites: Architecture.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
The caller creates SimulatorRuntime and AVStack. The runner validates hook stages, environments and command compatibility before reset. The simulator prepares the selected origin using the shared deployment tick budget, applies setup actions and captures the initial observation. Simulator-specific origin and capture behavior is described in Simulators.

AttackRuntime.setup receives its subscribed state and returns zero or more WorldAttackAction values. Actions register cleanup on the supplied ExitStack. See budget rules in Writing attacks.

Driving-history acquisition follows Past observations. The initialization event records past_steps and each historical observation's t and vehicle_state without sensor images.

docs.title: One decision
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as ClosedLoopRunner
    participant S as SimulatorRuntime
    participant A as AttackRuntime
    participant D as Driving system
    participant L as Recorder
    R->>S: reset selected origin
    S->>A: setup subscribed state
    S-->>R: initial capture and physical state
    R->>L: initialization event
    loop each decision
        R->>S: observe and state without advancement
        S-->>R: capture with composed world objects
        R->>A: step subscribed snapshots
        A-->>R: world, sensor and AVStack actions
        R->>R: sensor actions, then sensor environment
        R->>D: ObservationPipeline hooks and localization
        opt first decision
            R->>D: AVStack.reset(processed observation, past)
        end
        R->>D: AVStack(processed observation)
        D-->>R: produced command and component outputs
        R->>R: command actions, hooks and validation
        R->>S: queued world actions and step(executed command)
        S-->>R: post-state and next capture
        R->>R: keep the post-step context for AttackRuntime.stop
        R->>R: after_step feedback
        R->>L: record_step with actions and receipts
    end

ObservationPipeline processes a decision's input once. Decision zero uses that same processed observation for AVStack.reset and the first driving call. The localizer is not reset between them. World actions returned during a decision affect the next capture. Sensor and AVStack actions affect the current decision.

InsertObject is a WorldAttackAction with setup_ticks=0. A setup insertion appears in the first capture. A step insertion appears in the next capture. Camera composition precedes sensor actions, sensor environment and ObservationPipeline. Framework objects remain separate from native actors in WorldSnapshot.objects.

docs.title: Attack actions
docs.text:
Action Boundary WorldAttackAction Simulated-world changes SensorAttackAction Sensor capture changes, including camera, LiDAR, GNSS and IMU AVStackAttackAction Driving-system values from localization.pre through command

Sensor actions chain in issue order on independent data, preserving the original capture. Native wrappers retain calibration and acquisition metadata. Camera buffers remain RGB uint8. AVStackAttackAction rejects sensors.post, which remains a normal hook stage. A requested AVStack stage not reached in that decision makes the decision fail. Action stages are checked when actions are issued. Hook stages and command modes are checked when each run starts.

docs.title: Sensor views
docs.text: SensorView.camera and cam_from_world describe optical geometry when available. Optical axes are x right, y down, z forward. sensor_from_world describes the sensor body axes: x forward, y left, z up. It is None when the sensor pose is unavailable. The two transforms are distinct for cameras. SimulatorRuntime.sensors lists all views. camera_sensors lists its camera subset. SensorView.objects contains the inserted objects associated with the capture.

docs.title: CARLA LiDAR data
docs.text:
A CARLA LiDAR view contains an owned SensorCapture. raw_data holds packed float32 records x, y, z, intensity: four values, or 16 bytes, per point. These bytes use CARLA sensor axes: x forward, y right, z up. sensor_from_world uses the canonical body axes whose y points left.

Replacing the capture retains the native LidarData wrapper and its flipy setting. With flipy=True, the native exporter negates y. Supply replacement points in the original CARLA axes and preserve the capture's frame, timestamp and metadata.

This action shifts the points one meter forward:

import numpy as np
from avsectester.attack.runtime import SensorAttackAction
from avsectester.closed_loop.simulators.carla.sensors import SensorCapture

class ShiftLidarPointsAction(SensorAttackAction):
    sensor = "lidar"

    def apply(self, data, view):
        points = np.frombuffer(data.raw_data, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1, 4).copy()
        points[:, 0] += 1.0
        return SensorCapture(
            native_type=data.native_type,
            raw_bytes=points.tobytes(),
            frame=data.frame,
            timestamp=data.timestamp,
            metadata=dict(data.metadata),
        )

Return it from AttackRuntime.step. The runner supplies its current capture and SensorView.

docs.title: Hook stages
docs.text:
Hook(stage, handler) accepts a callable or an object with transform(value, context), where context is a StageContext. Handlers execute in registration order and consume preceding replacements. Adapters declare their supported stages. Unsupported stages fail before reset.

Stage Value simulator.setup None, native world setup simulator.step.pre and simulator.step.post None, before/after physical advancement sensors.post Observation localization.pre Observation, present only with a configured localizer localization.post StateEstimate observation Observation after localization perception.pre and perception.post CallInputs or component output, when declared tracking.pre and tracking.post CallInputs or component output, when declared planning.pre and planning.post CallInputs or component output, when declared control.pre and control.post CallInputs or component output, when declared policy.pre and policy.post Policy inputs or output, when declared command Control before execution render.pre and render.post CameraPoseRequest or rendered sensor, when declared

NuRec render.pre uses a 4×4 world_from_rig pose in CameraPoseRequest. The simulator.setup and simulator.step.* handlers return None. A component pre-hook returns CallInputs(args, kwargs). A post-hook returns the replacement output. NativeHook adapts an explicitly registered avstack-library hook.

docs.title: Contexts and lifecycle
docs.text:
OnlineContext exposes step, stage, sim_time, frame and optional subscribed observation and physical_state snapshots. record_output writes named output during a run. It carries no native runtime or time-advancing service. Bound AVStackAttackAction methods also receive the actual stage value.

StageContext exposes step, stage, sensor, physical_state, observation, control, run resources, rng and record_output. simulator_runtime and avstack expose borrowed native resources. Using native SDK objects ties a handler to that simulator or driving system.

Plugin.transform is required. reset(context), after_step(context) and close() are optional. after_step receives the next raw capture and the post-step clock. HookSet manages each handler owner's lifecycle once, including owners registered at several stages. Stateful handlers reset per run or are newly constructed. ObservationPipeline owns its localizer, whose lifecycle joins the other handlers.

docs.title: Randomness
docs.text: Sensor corruptions and hooks follow the randomness rules.

docs.title: Physical and model-visible records
docs.text:
StateEstimate contains the model-visible vehicle_state and ego_speed produced by localization. Physical snapshots remain separate from these values.

Record Fields and coordinates Observation t, frame, sensor_data, calibration, vehicle_state, ego_speed, route. Model-visible Control throttle, steer, brake, optional trajectory WorldSnapshot t, frame, vehicle_state, ego_speed, ego, actors, traffic_lights, objects. Physical ActorState world-from-actor pose, velocity, category, optional extent, local box_center and box_rotation Detection ego-frame position, full extent, yaw, category, score RecordedOutput name, copied value, decision step, stage, physical frame and t, sensor

ActorState.extent is full length, width and height in meters. None means unavailable. box_center is the actor-local box center. box_rotation is local roll/pitch/yaw in degrees. box_transform() combines these with the actor pose to return the world-from-box transform. Operations requiring dimensions report missing evidence when extent is None.

Detection uses the true capture-time ego frame, independently of driving localization: x forward, y left, z up, and yaw in radians. None detections means unsupported. An empty sequence means supported with no detections. WorldSnapshot.traffic_lights maps map control IDs to red, yellow, green, off or unknown. Simulator support is described in Simulators.

docs.title: RunLog
docs.text:
Registered dataclasses use JSON objects with _avsectester_type: "dataclass", type: "module:Class" and an encoded fields mapping. Mapping-key order is encoded separately. User mappings containing reserved serialization keys are escaped and round-trip unchanged. Payload retention defaults are defined in Configuration reference.

StepRecord separates raw_observation from model_observation, physical_pre from physical_post, and produced_command from executed_command. It also stores components, detections, actions, outputs, sensor_geometry, object_visibility and telemetry. Physical records retain framework object state.

Action requests and receipts distinguish requested changes from applied changes. A receipt's outcome is applied or not_applied, describing the action rather than its driving impact. Every receipt has a details mapping, empty when there is no detail. InsertionAttackAction adds rendered, reason, occlusion_source and ignored_occluders. InsertObject records object_id, asset_category and world_from_object.

StepRecord.object_visibility, the initialization event and RenderResult.object_visibility use object ID → camera name → ObjectVisibility. ObjectVisibility contains occlusion_source, ignored_occluders and visible_pixels. Visibility and composition behavior is described under Object visibility.

EventRecord captures initialization, termination and failure/cleanup information outside a decision. NuRec termination includes ground_contact_failures, counts by rejected ground-fit reason. A run ended by its terminate_when predicate records terminated_by_condition: true. RunLog.status distinguishes completed, failed, cancelled and incomplete runs.

Parquet stores typed scalar and nested values. Large arrays occupy payload shards. Payloads publish before referring record parts. Completion metadata publishes last. A crash leaves published parts readable and may lose an open part. Readers ignore *.open files.

SerializationRegistry handles JSON-compatible encoding and independent in-memory snapshots. Registered dataclasses reconstruct on read. Native values decode to ordinary data. Import and register user dataclasses before reading them. Missing registrations raise an error identifying the required registration. Framework registrations use type paths without eagerly importing SDKs.

This self-contained example stores a user record in a temporary directory:

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from avsectester.serialization import SerializationRegistry
from avsectester.runlog import Recorder, RunLog

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CameraCheck:
    sensor: str
    visible_pixels: int

registry = SerializationRegistry()
registry.register_dataclass(CameraCheck)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "run"
    with Recorder(path, registry=registry) as recorder:
        recorder.record_event("camera_check", value=CameraCheck("front", 12))
    restored = RunLog.read(path, registry=registry)
    assert restored.events[0].data["value"] == CameraCheck("front", 12)

Recorder supports bounded chunks and in-memory retention. Disabling in-memory retention requires a persistent output directory. Reader and recorder signatures are in the Python API.

docs.title: Failures and cleanup
docs.text: Unsupported environments are rejected during validation. Unsupported hook stages and command modes fail each run at its start, producing exit 1. A failing decision stops attack runtimes, records unapplied actions and cleans run resources. A requested action without an applied receipt is not evidence of an applied change. An incomplete log is not a completed run.
